entities.text: Jenny Clark We’ve seen an increase in voters over the last few years. People are starting to realize how important it is to vote in April.We also hold city council races in April. Those individuals are involved with making a lot more decisions that affect the average voter. Instead of moving elections to November and overwhelming voters with so much information that they have no time to figure out who to vote for because the ballot is so full, we should be working to educate voters on why April elections are important.The polls are open all day, and early and absentee voting are a thing. There is no excuse for someone not to vote.

entities.author: Sherry McNail
entities.text: #1. Absolutely untrue. I have always thought it was insane to expect high voter turnout multiple times per year. For so many reasons. I never could understand why often we make an effort to go vote for ONE item in April. It’s a waste of everyone’s time. Including but certainly not limited to the voters. those working the polling places and the school who have to close to accommodate. Why in the world would you think you have the right to speak for all of those supporting Senate Bill 1002? Would you like to see some personal chats dating back to well before 2022? You are categorically wrong. This is NOT new. #2. It already is. And we ALL know it. You can “say” it isn’t all you want but actions speak louder than words. #3. 🤷🏼‍♀️ It already is what it is. Why hide it? Seriously, why? Do you think Francis Howell School District is not widely known as a left district? As is Wentzville? #4. What’s new? Informational overload? Are you suggesting we couldn’t possibly handle being an informed voter if it means filling in another bubble or two? For working so hard to present yourself as non-political, you certainly have appeared political lately. You appear partisan. Our current board is widely known as partisan. Our district is widely viewed as partisan. The NEA is intrinsically partisan. Why else would you be worried about what time of year elections are held?

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | Hello Friends - Before Monday, May 4th I am asking you click this link to send your thoughts to Jefferson City. There is a hearing for Senate Bill 1002 happening Monday at 1pm. Senate Bill 1002 would move school board elections, school bond issues, and school tax levy votes to even year November elections FOR ST. CHARLES COUNTY ONLY. Everyone - click the link and send your opinion. https://witness.house.mo.gov/Default.aspx?noticeid=11680 If you can - come down to Jefferson City and show your opposition. Here is what I just sent: —— Missouri Legislators. I serve as the nonpartisan President of the Francis Howell School Board. I ask that you reject Senate Bill 1002 for the following reasons. 1- The stated desire to move to November for a larger voter turnout is false. Those supporting Senate Bill 1002 did not share that opinion when their endorsed school board candidates won. They changed their tune when their endorsed candidates lost three years in a row. Senate Bill 1002 isn’t about voter turnout. 2- Senate Bill 1002 is intentionally partisan, allowing candidates to run as Republican and Democrat. We need less partisan politics in schools, not more. St. Charles County would stand out across Missouri for its unique focus on partisanship instead of education. 3- Senate Bill 1002 would create Democrat districts and Republican districts. Regardless of our official high school mascots, each district would effectively be known by the political party of its current board members. We would be seen in the community as the St. Charles Donkeys, Wentzville Elephants, and others rotating back and forth based on the political winds. 4- November elections are filled with expensive state and federal races. The millions spent will flood mailboxes and inboxes with a cloud of information making it more difficult to inform voters on local school topics. If Senate Bill 1002 was good for education, why doesn’t every county want it? It is because no matter if you are red, blue, or purple, you know our school districts should not be partisan. Please, vote ‘NO’ on Senate Bill 1002. You don’t want it in your county. Regardless of what some legislators elected years ago say, we don’t want it in ours. Education Over Politics. | Nl75zkPBq.com

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | From our April Meeting 1- Warren Elementary Students led our Pledge of Allegiance and shared about their fantastic leadership/goal setting program. 2. We received a financial report that further laid the groundwork for next year’s budget proposal that is presented in June. 3. We learned that Jefferson City lawmakers plan to not fully fund the formula for public schools next year. We predicted this could happen so our current budget was not based on Jeff City funding the full amount. However, the actual amount they will fund is even lower than our conservative estimate. We will share the specific number shortly as this news had just been released. We do know it will cause millions in lost revenue immediately. More information to follow. 4. We also learned that there are other bills in Jeff City that could lead $6M or more in lost revenue. More information to follow. 5. We approved a few administrative regulations. 6. Attentional Barnwell Families - We approved a very small land transfer to the fire department to build a new firehouse and replace the current one. The construction and placement of the new building will lead to improved traffic flow for buses and parents picking up their kids. The new layout will better utilize the traffic light and will lead to improved traffic for Becky David dropoff as well. This decision will also lead to improved fire protection coverage for these two schools and the surrounding residents. 7. Strategic Plan Quarterly Update highlighted the work happening in all four pillars. Jus a few updates: Education - New reading curriculum is in use and new reading resources have been approved. Teacher/Staff: Climate Survey finalized allowing new information to be addressed. Financial Stewardship: Saved $300,000 by utilizing a 1:1 tech distribution model for middle and high school students vs the previous classroom based model. Safety and Security: Implemented new ‘Raptor’ system that scans the driver’s license of every visitor to make sure no one is near kids who shouldn’t be. 8. Prop RT was not on our agenda because we defeated it. We didn’t have to make plans to cut $4M (year one) in staffing, benefits, and services because you all created a nonpartisan/bipartisan coalition and beat that terrible bill 59-41. Thank you everyone for reading. The update was a little later this month due to a college visit. | FspWd0DDVS.com

entities.author: Jason Abrams
entities.text: Castillo Elementary in the heart of FHSD has seen first hand the outcome of boys becoming girls and then trying to go into the girls bathroom. My daughter's came home off bus just 4 years ago the first day after Christmas break (sorry...called winter break now) and told wife and me how a boy in their grade (4th or 5th at the time) left for break as a boy and came back as a girl and that this "new" girl will be using the girls restroom. The school stance was that if any kids had issues, those kids should use the nurses restroom...Basically entire school had to change to adapt to this newly presented girl...issue resolved itself within a very short timeframe and did so without violence and without the parents really doing much (many many parents protested). Right, wrong or indifferent, what got the kid out of school on its own was simply natural consequences....kids avoid odd and weird people so the kids themselves just completely ignored (some did shame and I agree thats wrong) this transgender to the point that this he/she got so depressed (I guess) that his/her parents withdrew him/her from school. Only took few weeks. Gone my Feb. Not one act of violence...in a kids world, social interaction is vital. In this case, there was basically a school wide unified unofficial stance by almost all kids as they just ignored and avoided the he/she. That was the most devastating action that likely resulted in kid leaving the school. Teachers noticed and even tried to encourage interaction simply on a human level but all that did was get the he/she realize it was forced socialization and that likely hurt more. Lesson is...While you can do want you with your own life and body, there are consequences because everyone else also has free will to do and respond how they want or in this case, just ignore. The issues transgender people currently have is the same exact issue that the flat earth people have. Lack of evidence to support their stance. There are to many documented scientific and proven facts that support the exact opposite of what they are saying/believing so it kills any credibility arguments they pose once reviewed by people who are logical in thoughts and educated. As parents of then 4th and 5th graders, we had to sit our girls down and explain how its ok for those who want to be transgender and they can do/be them. We also then explained it is ok to be their friend but my kids need to realize that a mental issue exist and my kids have same equal rights to belive they are not right in the head, do not have to socialize with them, do not have to conform to transgender thoughts, do not need to help forward the LGBTQ+++ (Whatever the 25% of alphabet and symbols they use is) cause and that any alphabet soup involvement with my children and wife will only be while I am in same room watching and hearing 100% of the interaction so that I can immediately step in to implement corrective measures when and as I should deem it necessary (my free will and bring a protective parent)Its ok to believe what you want. Most laws and norms are needed and good but Its not ok to force print your personal beliefs onto others and then forcefully reqire they comply. I believe that someone tried that and WW2 happened, not to mention most other conflicts throughout human history have started by someone trying to force others to comply.

entities.author: Steven Blair For Francis Howell School Board
entities.text: Francis Howell Teachers, Staff, & Parents Because We Defeated Prop RT: Our next Board meeting will NOT include a conversation about cutting $4,000,000 from our budget next year. Our next Board meeting will NOT include setting a date to decide which benefits we will need to take away from staff and what services/activities we will need to take away from students. Our next Board meeting will NOT need to scrap our Strategic Plan in place for a plan to keep our heads above water as we prepare for a $54M funding loss in five years. Instead, our next board meeting will continue to focus on providing The BEST Education for ALL Students. I will continue to do everything I can for the students. When necessary, I will fight for them. Fighting for students means fighting for the teachers and staff who benefit the students. We aren’t where I want to be, yet, but we will get there. We fought Prop RT and we won. We will fight the next Prop RT, no matter what it is called or when it shows up. We will build nonpartisan and bipartisan coalitions and we will win. Thank you to all the voters who voted NO on Prop RT. I see all the love you have for our students, teachers, staff, and parents. You changed the trajectory of Francis Howell. Time to get to work pursuing our large, inspirational Strategic Plan for 2030.

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | We Did It! We successfully defeated Prop RT!! 60% to 40% is more than I could imagine! St. Charles County overwhelmingly stood up for Schools, Libraries, Fire and EMS Services, and the Developmental Disabilities Resource Board. It looks like St. Charles County might be one of the only counties in the state to defeat Senate Bill 3 (Prop RT). What this means Schools don’t have to start planning budget cuts that would increase class sizes and reduce how we compensate staff. The St. Charles City-County Library isn’t talking about cutting staff, hours, services, or branches. Fire and EMS services are protected. The 26 organizations funded by the DDRB aren’t discussing which services for adults and kids with disabilities need to cut. Thank you to all the Bipartisan and Non-partisan voices that came together to defeat Prop RT. Prop RT would have been Really Terrible for St. Charles County. Because of your vote, your voice, and your volunteering we defeated Prop RT. Thank You! Thank You! Thank You! | l81Qq.com

entities.author: Dennis Fischer
entities.text: I can support all the things that are listed here and still vote yes on Prop RT. Taxing entities are out of control and Prop RT is a small start at requiring them to be better stewards of our tax revenue. Prop RT defunds NO ONE, it simply slows the automatic revenue increases created by rapidly increasing property values. As far as the sales tax proposals, not a single taxing entity has outlined a funding gap, just asking for more money. The tax payers cannot keep pace with the tax takers, you’ll never be able to give them enough revenue.

entities.author: Dwight Mullen
entities.text: It's simple math... Between 2023 - 2025 property values went up 37% in St Charles County. In that same time period, the cost of inflation to Property Tax funded entities only went up by 7%. Fire, EMS, and Schools are currently operating on a 30% revenue increase windfall (actual spending went up 3.5% per their published budgets). New home construction is still booming in this county and will continue to increase the budget funding for these entities. Anyone telling you that Schools, Disabled Services, Fire, Ambulance, and others will lose money due to freezing Property Tax assessments at the 2025 levels is either Grossly Misinformed, or outright lying to you.

entities.author: Karen Sieve
entities.text: I share your concern for our schools, developmental disabilities population, libraries and emergency services if Prop RT passes. Our school district receives 75 percent of its funding from property taxes, and we stand to lose $54 Million in five years. Many of our students with intellectual and developmental disabilities and their families also receive support from DDRB, which helps them thrive and be successful. If Prop RT passes, cuts in services, programs and jobs are inevitable, and it's our kids, families and property values that will pay the price.

entities.author: Denny Watson Obl Osb
entities.text: With Proposition RT on our April 7th ballot both Saint Charles County and Saint Charles City in their current Newsletter Articles have put forth what this Property Tax Freeze might have on the budgets for both the county, school districts and municipalities. These are all somewhat hypothetical, yes, it will change how these entities receive tax dollars but it is not all doom and gloom.What Proposition RT will do is force all these taxing entities to come directly to the voters for future revenue increases thus letting the public decide if this is what they want to fund.This is the way it should work and also makes sure that the tax dollars are used in a way that has approval of the residents not developers.All we have to do is look at the issues with data centers to see why this is a great proposition.I live in Orchard Farm School District and over the past five years the school district came directly to the residents for revenue on specific projects. The school district did a great job on educating the residents on the issues so much so that the bond and tax issued passed with ease.Don’t buy into the gloom and doom that is being spued think of it as additional controls over our tax dollars. It is good to have the residents vote on these issues and force a clear path for those entities that want our dollars.

It’s a way for the people who earn more to pay less. Based on my spending, it’ll cost me another $400-700/annual in these extra sales taxes. Property taxes would be around $150 annually. Sales taxes are also tied to the cost of each item - which has already increased due to tariffs and rising fuel prices will cause the price of things to go up. Property taxes 110% are a tax on the “rich” because they tend to have more expensive houses. Larger houses and larger plots of land.

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | March Board Meeting Update. 1- Our Pledge of Allegiance was led by the Becky David Elementary Sign Language Club. The club exists to build a community of students who build friendships through conversational sign language with hearing impaired students. 2- Superintendent Mark Delaney shared that his parents are hearing impaired. He is especially appreciative of the great work happening at Becky David under the leadership of Ms. Brewer. 3-We celebrated the Barnwell Robotics Team ‘Mighty Minors’ who won State and will be competing at Internationals. 4 - We approved and signed the contract with teachers through our negotiations with our teachers union. Significantly, there will be a Part-Time Release President. The union will pay for the salary and benefits for the half where the union president works on union business. The district will pay for the half when the teacher is teaching. 5- We approved a list of agenda items that included receipt of a $268,xxx check from the Developmental Disabilities Resource Board. The DDRB provides funding that helps us provide 1:1 personnel for special need students. 6-We received and approved a financial report that again shared the severe damage Prop RT will cause. Francis Howell will lose $4M in funding in year one and $54M in funding over five years. Loss of funding from the DDRB would be on top of those numbers. 7-When asked what would happen if Prop RT passed, Superintendent Delaney shared that the district will have stakeholder conversations to see where we would need to cut the $4M. 8-We voted and approved updates to Policy 6310 which provides guidance for book acquisitions. We maintained the ability for parents to decide what books their kids can read. We also maintained the language allowing for new books to be presented to the public as an information item at each board meeting. We removed detailed language that was deemed unnecessary as the rest of the policy language already requires age appropriateness related to violence, drug use, sexual content, etc. 9- We voted and approved a Safe Schools Curriculum. This was created by Francis Howell employees. It is based on Missouri Standards and provides a district-wide framework for building safer schools. I am very proud of the work that went into this curriculum. It will help us get closer to having 100% of students (and staff) feel safe at school. 10- The Board Members Comments agenda item included differences of opinion, which is an expected aspect of school boards. Thank you for reading and being involved in the great work happening at Francis Howell. Also, Follow ‘Vote NO on Prop RT’ and Vote NO on Prop RT on April 7th. | g4qUBvIs.com

entities.author: Sherry Burnside
entities.text: I wouldn’t mind paying school taxes embedded into the property taxes and real estate taxes IF I could experience educated kids…..they are disrespectful…can’t make change even when the computer screen tells them what to return to me…..don’t know how our government works…don’t know where the government gets their money…..etc. etc. I am tired of paying taxes….yes there are Social Security raises but guess what…the Medicare premiums go up at the same time…..leaving you with no increase in the net amount or minimal increases in the net. Yes my income is “fixed”. Take out the idiotic spending and go back to the basics….reading …writing….math. And I don’t mean the new math…..2+2 is 4…period. When I do encounter kids with common sense and smarts….they are usually the ones not going to a public school. I don’t think seniors should pay any taxes after age 65. Most of us worked hard for 40 years….we believed in it. We showed up even though it might have been hard. We didn’t ask for special privileges in our school years. We didn’t need counseling …nor safe spaces…nor litter boxes…nor zoom classes. I don’t know what this RT bill says…I just know I am tired of handing over my money to anyone or anything that is not accountable to the people.

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | Carl is a regular at FHSD Board Meetings. He has earned the reputation of following facts wherever they take him. Hear this thoughts below: Vote NO April 7 on Prop RT. To the Voters and Taxpayers of St. Charles County, I have been following school finances closely for ten years. I am a fiscal conservative and want to lay out my concerns with Prop RT: 1. I am OPPOSED to Prop RT as it will cause significant reductions in local property tax revenue for local school districts (and other taxing districts) without any offsetting alternative tax increases. The Senior Citizen Property Tax Freeze previously enacted cost the FHSD ~$1 million last year. Prop RT is expected to cost as much as $4 million the first year and increase cumulatively from there. 2. I believe the education of our citizens is vital to a fully functioning and free society. I also believe that the costs for educating our children should be borne by most citizens. 3. To be clear, I’m not one who believes that school districts deserve unlimited funding or that higher funding levels will necessarily correlate with higher student outcomes. I was one of a handful of voters that successfully defeated the last tax levy proposal in 2018. 4. This ballot proposal appears to me as “a solution looking for a problem”. The premise of this ballot proposal must be that taxes are escalating way too much and people can’t afford them. Below are my arguments against this premise. 5. Prop RT is basically an expansion of the Senior Property Tax Freeze to all property owners. The Senior Property Tax Freeze is flawed for the following reasons: a. The Hancock Amendment has been in place for many years and limits property tax increases to the Consumer Price Increase (CPI) or 5%, whichever is less. This protects taxpayers from unusually large increases in taxes simply because property values are escalating more than inflation. b. The Missouri Property Tax Credit (Circuit Breaker) provides a tax credit up to $1,100 for homeowners (couples) earning less than $34,000 per year. If the legislature wanted to provide additional relief to the poorest taxpayers, they could have simply increased the existing credit and eligibility level. However, in so doing the legislature would have to had pay for it, whereas the cost of the Senior Property Tax Freeze falls to all the local taxing jurisdictions. c. The other fallacy is that seniors are on fixed incomes and can’t afford any increases in taxes: i. Social Security recipients receive annual cost of living adjustments based on CPI ii. Public Pension recipients generally receive annual cost of living adjustments iii. Private Pension recipients generally do not receive increases, but very few people are entitled to these now. iv. Those with 401k / IRA accounts (replacing many private pensions) have benefitted immensely as the stock market historically returns 10% per year, significantly more than the CPI. v. We need to expand the tax base (local, state, & federal) instead of contracting it as these amendments do. Everyone needs “to have a little skin in the game”. 6. Prop RT takes the Senior Property Tax Freeze and expands it to all taxpayers. In addition to the issues identified above with the Senior Property Tax Freeze, Prop RT may introduce even more concerns: a. Missouri will have different taxation rules between neighboring counties. St. Louis County does not have an April ballot property tax proposal like St. Charles does. So, what will happen if taxes are frozen in St. Charles but not in St. Louis County? i. Will teachers lean toward St. Louis County school districts since they will be better able to pay annual increases? ii. Will parents tend to migrate to St. Louis County since the schools will be better funded? b. You’ll end up after several years if Prop RT is approved where neighbors with similar houses will pay significantly different property taxes, for the same level of services (schools, ambulance, library, etc). How is that fair? c. Again, with the potential passage of this flawed ballot proposal, will it depress home sales as homeowners won’t want to give up the accumulated credits from the freeze and expose themselves to higher taxes on a different house. If sales are depressed, will this not hurt local businesses that support home sales such as realtors, lenders, furniture and home improvement stores? d. Similar to the Senior Property Tax Freeze, all accumulated credits could be lost if the property owner fails to renew the application one time, thus resulting in a significant increase in their tax bill. This is poor policy. Thank you for taking the time to understand this important issue for St. Charles County and I hope you will join me in defeating this terrible ballot measure. Carl Suhre 2/27/2026 Vote NO April 7 on Prop RT. | eNYTOs2.com

entities.author: Steven Blair For Francis Howell School Board
entities.text: I have heard some misconceptions from Thursday BOE Technology Update. We currently use a classroom approach to distribute chromebooks to high school and middle school students. This does require each classroom to have a higher number of chromebooks to match the hour with the largest class size. We are shifting to a personal chromebook model where each high school and middle school student will be assigned their own chromebook. Thursday’s Technology Update included these advantages to the change. 1- Money Savings - The personal chromebook model costs less than the classroom model. 2- Students can bring their personal chromebook home allowing for greater access to homework and Canva. 3- Students can more easily navigate the chromebook, as shared by Thursday’s student representative. This change in distribution does not mean students will be on technology more than before. It is simply a change in how chromebooks are assigned. This change provides greater efficiency for students and saves money for taxpayers. Win-Win. Transparency is only effective if it is connected to open, understandable communication. I hope this helps. Please feel free to ask questions. I’ll do my best to answer them.

entities.author: Dennis Fischer
entities.text: Stephanie Cooley Rittgers Its not correct to say that that revenues will be frozen if Prop RT passes. There will still be the commercial and industrial property bi-annual reassessments and new construction as well as residential property being resold and then reset to new value. There is also nothing that says the school district can’t ask for future tax increases or bond issue, they would just need to explain why they need additional funds and personally I think that should always be the case. Did you know that the ambulance district estimates the sales tax (PropEMS) will bring in over $40 million additional dollars? Thats just about the same amount as they currently collect in property tax. The fire districts will collect the same percentage increases. This windfall of money to these taxing entities is unsustainable.

entities.author: Dennis Fischer
entities.text: The school district can’t add a sales tax onto the April ballot to sidestep the property tax freeze but unfortunately the school district doesn’t live in a bubble and their continued cries to vote the property tax freeze down will effect residents for decades to come. St. Charles County Ambulance District and all the fire districts in St. Charles County have added sales tax propositions to the April ballot, seems odd that they all need additional revenue at the same time. The ambulance district has projected an increase in revenue from the sales tax of over 40 million dollars almost doubling what they currently get from property taxes. The fire districts will receive similar revenue increases. Now imagine the windfall they will all receive if the property tax freeze is defeated and they all continue to get their automatic increases each year. I’m a proponent of good schools, ambulance and fire service but at some point I won’t be able to keep my house because of escalating taxes.

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | A Word About Book Challenges Thursday’s Board of Education Meeting will have a couple items related to book challenges. 1- Admin will share that district libraries and admin have reviewed a list of book challenges. An initial 100 book challenges, became a list of 53 book challenges that completed the steps in Regulation 6341. 14 of those books were not in our libraries of had been previously weeded. That leaves 39 books. For multiple reasons, our library media specialists recommend that 22 books be weeded from the high school libraries. This leaves 17 books that library media specialists believe should be retained. The Board of Education will vote on whether to retain or remove these 17 books at Thursday’s meeting. 2- Regulation Change 6341. At the January Board meeting, the Board recognized that the details of 6341 were causing organizational problems leading to one board member calling 6341 ‘broken.’ At the February Board meeting, admin is presenting a series of changes to 6341 that have gone through the policy committee. Due to the risk of another large scale challenging of books, this will be presented for 1st read, 2nd read, and vote. One proposed change poses a limit of five book challenges district wide and a maximum ofnone book challenge per school at a given time. Another would require the person challenging the book to attend the first meeting of the book’s challenge committee. 3- Wording for 6310 - A change in policy 6310 is being presented for 1st read so it better matches the other book challenging policy. 4- District admin will share the multiple steps already in place that allows a parent to control/determine what their kids can read. | Pw3EhcxmF.com

entities.text: If you haven’t noticed it appears that every fire district in St.Charles county and the ambulance district has added a 1% sales tax onto the April ballot. I suspect this is in response to SB3. Rather than waiting to see if SB3 passes and what impact it would actually have it appears they’re being proactive. You might want to imagine the revenue windfall these taxing entities will receive should SB3 fail and the sales tax propositions pass.

They would be forced to eliminate wasteful spending like the PROP S fund mismanagement for which the district received a "POOR" rating from the state auditor.

entities.author: Ewan Ross
entities.text: Jeff Snodgrass overall revenue increase for the district is capped by the Hancock amendment.This means while your own tax may increase significantly the overall revenue for property tax (all residence and commercial) cannot exceed either inflation or 5%, whichever is lower.As such while it hurts at a personal level when you get such a big increase, the district doesn’t actually see that same increase in revenue.The 5% option on SB3 would have actually made things better for everyone - rather than capping the entire revenue stream it would have protected individuals from massive jumps (there may have been some dip in revenue, but not a whole stop)

entities.author: Dennis Fischer
entities.text: I'm not advocating for the decline of education but I do believe that a consistent cycle of adding/increasing revenue streams is unsustainable. I would be much more inclined to give your "reading professional" careful consideration if not for the multi million dollar athletic facilities I see everywhere in school districts, could we maybe have used a few of those dollars for that position? Don't get me wrong, I love sports but not at the cost of basic education. The point I'm trying to make here is that maybe a careful examination of how the district is currently allocating their funds needs to be considered before just continuing the current practice of escalating the budget. Also, please don't use the tired old excuse of "we can't be blamed for the fiscal incompetence of previous administrations". Questionable spending has been a hallmark of Francis Howell as long as I can remember.

entities.author: Steven Blair For Francis Howell School Board
entities.text: One more piece I loved the Resolution Against Racism. It is one of the reasons we chose to move into Francis Howell. I have been focused on the multiple ways we can apply our anti-discrimination policy and improve culture. This includes a commitment to this statement on culture in our strategic plan: (By 2030) “Celebrated for the work we’ve done on culture, morale and ensuring all members of our community feel safe and welcome.” These are just pretty words if they are not followed by action. I am sharing that there is action happening to make this a reality in Francis Howell. There is value to having a resolution. That can be discussed. I am certain that the actions are more important than words and invite an ongoing conversation towards good action.

I am sharing that there is action happening to make this a reality in Francis Howell. There is value to having a resolution. That can be discussed. I am certain that the actions are more important than words and invite an ongoing conversation towards good action.

entities.author: Steven Blair For Francis Howell School Board
entities.text: Happy Black History Month! Our Black students and staff are a gift to the district and the surrounding community. We all benefit from learning Black History, both the courageous and the horrific. People are quick to call themselves an ALLY. It’s important for each person to pause and realize that we aren’t there, yet. In Francis Howell, this means advancing a culture that black students, families, and staff want to belong to. It includes fixing the disparity in reading and math scores amongst our black students which systemically resemble other districts. These are two key parts of our district’s strategic plan that we are allocating time and attention to improve until we can proudly say that every student is getting the best education. For the courage we see, we celebrate. For the fairness that is missing, we work. We aren’t there, yet.

entities.text: Amber Fakebook Hello Amber. I am not opposed to tax cuts. However, I am opposed to defunding fire districts, ambulance districts, libraries, the Developmental Disabilities Resource Board and schools. I wish they could freeze inflating costs to match freezing revenue. If Senate Bill 3 passed, but they found another way to replace the funding we wouldn’t be fighting SB 3. Looking at just the money, SB 3 is very bad for kids and their education. There are job openings for reading professionals who we are currently now filling in fear of SB 3 passing, for just one example. Losing $4 million in funding in year one and an estimated $54 million after five years paints a grim picture on how many jobs will be left unfilled and how many kids will miss out on a better education because of it. I support every kid having the best public education. Therefore, I wholeheartedly oppose Senate Bill 3.

entities.text: Dennis Fischer I appreciate your comment. Other entities can use sales tax increases to offset the loss of revenue caused by Senate Bill 3. School districts have not been allowed that option. My language is careful not to call SB3 a tax decrease. However, largely flattening/freezjng the tax revenue results in a drop of funding for all these entities. If SB3 could magically flatten our cost for electricity, food, health insurance, buses, etc we wouldn’t need to oppose it. I understand the concern about financial management in Francis Howell due to concerns about choices from years ago. I understand and do does administration. It is why we are incredibly transparent with our finances, especially compared to our districts. Lessons learned the hard way are still lessons learned. Additionally, damaging a kids’ education because of a disagreement over a choice made by adults years ago would also not be fair to that kid. In a very real, practical sense our district needs to hire another reading professional to help kids read at a particular school. If Senate Bill 3 passes, we will not fill that position. If it fails, we will. We can take the example of that one position and magnify it. Senate Bill 3 would cause a $4 million loss of funding in year one and $20 million a year loss in funding in year 5. That’s a lot of services that could help kids that we won’t be able to offer. Thanks for taking the time to read my way too long reply.

entities.author: Dennis Fischer
entities.text: I’m not quite sure that it’s fair to say FH will be losing money as much as just not growing as fast as usual. I also have concerns about the spending track record at FH. Also consider that some of the other taxing entities, fire districts for one, are currently looking into creating new revenue streams that would sidestep SB3 and my understanding is that they intend to move forward with these revenue streams regardless of SB3, consider that windfall. I think the tax escalation needs to be controlled, where does it stop? When we’re all taxed out of our homes?

entities.text: John N Debbie Maneke I think the reason so many of us are concerned with this upcoming vote is that there’s is NOT a way to replace the income that is going to be lost-if we freeze the money coming in (and for FHSD 78% of the budget from these taxes-that’s the way MO has structured school funding), it’s effectively a pay cut. I will be voting against this because I want the ambulance or fire to show up T my housing I need it. I want the children in our district to receive quality public education-these are the folks who will be the doctors, nurses, engineers, lawyers, teachers, police officers, tradesman, etc of the future-we all will be better when the kids are well educated! I want those with disabilities to be able to have the resources the need to be functional members of society. We all rise when we take care of them!

And research has shown time and time again that higher sales tax hurt those with smaller incomes this on fixed incomes. The people who benefit are the extremely.

entities.author: Holly Snyder
entities.text: Jeff Snodgrass public education impacts you in so many ways. Your future nurse, doctor, dentist, firefighter, police officer, farmer, and so many others will use public education. This isn't a simple budget issue and do more with less. Can you maintain your home on the same budget you did 20 years ago? Would you accept the same salary you did 20 years ago? That is what this freeze will do to public schools. It is freezing funding. Costs will still increase for utilities, gas for busses, textbooks and curriculum, athletic equipment. People will likely be laid off. Class sizes will rise. Test scores will lower.

entities.author: John N Debbie Maneke
entities.text: I've always wonder why we pay Personal Property tax, and when did it start? I paid taxes on the car when it was purchased, why do I continue to pay a tax for the privilege of owning it? I appreciate that we need to support these entities but these taxes are going to price us retired folks out of our homes and make us sell our vehicles. If the current tax structure is changed where will the money to support these entities come from?

entities.author: Steven Blair For Francis Howell School Board
entities.text: Jeff Snodgrass Hello Jeff. I understand. If there was some other sort of funding that was going to replace what is lost, I wouldn’t argue. I like a tax cut as much as anyone else. However, the impact of SB 3 on Francis Howell alone would be catastrophic. A $4 million loss of revenue in year one alone would lead to leaving certain positions open that otherwise would have helped kids read, etc. By year five, it will be a $20 million loss in revenue, and $54 million total estimated loss over the five years. 75% of our budget is salary and benefits. It is impossible to cut that much from a budget without it costing jobs, extracurricular activities, and routine maintenance on our most 3 million sq.ft. of buildings.Right now, our tax levy is $3.97. Compare that with the districts around us and you can see that we are doing a lot of good with less than what other school districts are working with. I appreciate your interest. I hope this information is helpful.

entities.author: Karen Sieve
entities.text: Jeff Snodgrass if it sounds too good to be true, that’s because it is. It’s important to think this through. How will schools, libraries, fire departments, ambulance services be funded? How will this impact our property values? Our sales taxes will increase & be regressive, meaning the poor, the middle class and the elderly will bear the burden of higher prices at the grocery store. Especially since the governor also has plans to eliminate state income tax. And last year, Missouri also eliminated the capital gains tax. The money has to come from somewhere. The Missouri Budget Project estimate that to fully replace income tax, the state sales tax would need to rise from its current 3% to as high as 11.5%.When combined with local city and county taxes, shoppers in some areas could see a total sales tax rate of 17% to 19% on everyday purchases. Services like haircuts, lawn care, etc. will be taxed.High sales taxes near state borders (particularly in the Kansas City and St. Louis metros) could drive consumers to shop in Kansas or Illinois, hurting Missouri small businesses.

entities.author: Andrew Stuecken
entities.text: Karen Sieve it's a crazy plan. I agree with everything you said. Many of the other states that do not have income tax either 1) have a much lower annual operating budget than MO(SD, WY) or 2) are able to have reasonable sales tax rates because it is funded heavily by out of state tourists bringing money into those states(FL, TN, NV, TX). We do not have the same benefits as those states, so that higher sales tax burden will be absorbed almost entirely by Missourians, especially in lower and middle classes. Senate Bill 3 is dangerous for public schools in the state, and the removal of income tax takes it another step farther. Even conservative board members should be able to acknowledge to financial impact it will have, and be able to openly oppose. entities.author: Karen Sieve
entities.text: Why wouldn’t board members that support public education share the facts about Senate Bill 3? Cuts to property taxes and personal property taxes, combined with the Governor’s plan to cut income taxes will have catastrophic impacts on public schools, libraries, fire departments, and ambulance services. If that’s their plan, I’d like to hear what the plan is for funding these services. Our sales taxes will skyrocket & be regressive, meaning the poor and middle class will bear the burden of higher prices at the grocery store. Also services like haircuts, lawn care, etc. will be taxed. Maybe even prescription drugs. The Missouri Budget Project estimate that to fully replace income tax, the state sales tax would need to rise from its current 3% to as high as 11.5%. When combined with local city and county taxes, shoppers in some areas could see a total sales tax rate of 17% to 19% on everyday purchases. High sales taxes near state borders (particularly in the Kansas City and St. Louis metros) could drive consumers to shop in Kansas or Illinois, hurting Missouri small businesses. It’s my understanding that nine other states have cut income taxes. One state still has capital gains tax, which we do not. Even if the state does not cut income taxes, SB 3 will have a catastrophic impact on Francis Howell and other public school districts. We all need to continue to bang the drum and spread the word about the impacts of these irresponsible proposals.

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | Here is a quick update from last night’s meeting 1- We followed the lead of four Daniel Boone students who led our Pledge of Allegiance. 2- We celebrated two groups at Hollenbeck who are mentoring students and seeing results. 3- We approved a Facility Master Plan that we have been developing for nearly a year. This approves a general path forward and did not approve anybody action, project, budget, etc within it. 4- We approved the Vacation Station and Early Childhood Center plan. I’ll say more later, but this is significant. Due to the great work of Dr. Amy St. John, Julie Walsh, and Dr. Will Vanderpool we are able to - Keep and expand full day preschool - Keep preschool rates the same, or almost the same. - Improve our class size ratio for special need preschool students This didn’t look possible a few months ago. 5- Book Challenges - We discussed the impact of having 38 book challenges at once. Admin requested that we first look to see if our current librarians would choose to retain those books and then present the plan in February. If there are a large number of books on that list that the librarians and other admin see the educational value in keeping, admin will bring those books to the Board, likely at the February meeting. This is allowed in Policy 6341 and would save countless hours of staff time and $2000-$4000 of taxpayer dollars that would have been spent buying the books for the committee. We also discussed how Policy 6341 is “broken.” We asked admin to come up with some efficiency change recommendations to share at our February meeting. It’s signifcant that admin will be presenting changes and not board members. 6- Senate Bill 3- Board members shared different opinions on whether a school board should tell others how to vote. The result is that we did not unanimously agree to state that we oppose SB3. More on this later. Thank you everyone for continuing to care about Francis Howell. Our best days are ahead of us. w nyeser | BDn7P.com

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | Board Meeting Preview- Lots happening this Thursday. We have developed an agenda that helps us pursue our Strategic Plan. It includes 1- Facility Master Plan - We will vote on whether to approve the Facility Master Plan to guide us over going forward. A vote to approve the Plan will not approve any action within the Plan. The vote is to move in the general direction laid out in the Plan. 2-Preschool and Early Childhood Tuition Rate- We have good news to share. Full Day Preschool will continue and will grow from seven to eight rooms without any tuition increase. We will also provide better teacher-student ratio for our special need preschool students for half day preschool with some openings for half day preschool peer models. All half day preschool will happens at our three ECC locations. Full day preschool will happen at four elementary schools. This is a far better solution than we thought was possible a few months ago. You will hear how we arrived here at the meeting (Spoiler alert: we have brilliant, creative admin who care a lot about kids). 3-Strategic Plan- We will receive our quarterly update about our 2030 Strategic Plan, celebrating what we have already done and discussing next steps. 4- Book Challenge Recommendation. - The Book Challenge Policy 6341 approved in the summer of 2025 was not designed to process 38 book challenges at one time. We will hear admin’s recommendation on how we can maintain the spirit of 6341 while suggesting procedural changes for efficiency. 5- Senate Bill 3 Discussion. - The Board will discuss how we will communicate our opinion about SB3 based on all the facts we have learned about its impact to Francis Howell students, staff, and schools. SB 3 is on the Apri Ballot and will lead to a $4 million loss in revenue in year one and a $20 million estimated loss in year five. We invite you to attend in person, sign up to speak, or watch online. Thank you for staying involved in seeing all the great things happening in Francis Howell. | h7TjPQyt.com

entities.author: Ewan Ross
entities.text: 6341 allows for the superintendent to simply move books directly to the board. I propose in the spirit of maintaining staff morale, resources and community trust the following course of action - The board pledge to read each book, allot a timeframe in which all the books must be read (based on 100-400 pages per week) and return at a meeting after that timeframe has been advanced to vote on the books either individually or en masse. It is unreasonable to shift the burden to admin or staff given their already overwhelming workloads. In the meantime rewrite the policy (both challenge and 6310) to cover such dishonest behavior from politically motivated actors.

In the meantime rewrite the policy (both challenge and 6310) to cover such dishonest behavior from politically motivated actors.

entities.text: For 4 - while challenging books is a right granted to patrons, so is sunshining information. Anyone challenging a book should deposit the equivalent funds to cover costs (charged hourly) for admin and teacher time for a challenge committee. If a challenge succeeds the district should return said funds, if it fails the funds should be retained. This would stop spurious or malicious challenges while allowing valid challenges. Policy 6310 should have been rewritten in April/May of 2025. The prior board wrote bad policy which, if adhered to by the letter of the law, will likely remove a lot of material due to it being overly restrictive (potentially removing books which are on AP English reading lists, thus damaging educational standards and further undermining the district’s reputation) That the prior board majority were too stupid to write policy that was internally coherent (challenge policy and 6310 are not in line with each other) shouldn’t be allowed to harm the district’s reputation. The more permissive set of rules should be followed, or all challenges should be put on hold until we have policy not written by idiots.

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | Board Meeting Preview Our monthly meeting is this Thursday. The Board agenda becomes public the Monday before every Board meeting here: https://go.boarddocs.com/mo/fhsdmo/Board.nsf/Public This month we will: 1- Celebrate FHHS Cheerleading for winning State. 2- Receive the clean report regarding our annual audit. 3-Approve travel requests for teachers to improve teaching instruction across the district. 4 - Receive a check from Sodexo, our food services vendor. 5- Receive our monthly financial update that will include information about how Senate Bill 3 would take away $4 million in funding from FHSD in year one and $20 million in year five, if the ballot measure passes in April. 6- Vote on the book ‘Viral: The Fight Against AIDS in America’ by Ann Bausum. Because the book challenge committee formed for that book missed having quorum for a meeting, the decision regarding that book moves to the Board. The Board will decide to either keep the book at the middle school level, move it to the high school level, or choose to remove it from all school libraries. The meeting will include other moments of recognizing the great work happening in our district and other Board conversations about directing the needed resources around our strategic plan. You can join us in person or watch us online. You can also sign up to be part patron comments, as well. | Fqej2kWgo.com

entities.author: Matthew Paul
entities.text: Banning books because they contain the offensive word is just sanitizing history. The context that word was used in must not be forgotten. In his book "America’s Education Deficit and the War on Youth," Henry Giroux warns that when we erase the evidence of systemic violence and racism, we strip young people of the tools they need to understand the present. We leave them with a past that is a lie. If a student reads a novel placed in the Jim Crow era and feels sickened by the language used against Black Americans, that is not a failure of the school. That is a moral success. That discomfort is the sound of a conscience waking up. Do not rob them of that essential experience.

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | From Thursday’s Board Meeting 1- We heard that our Core Values have been displayed at all our schools. View them here. https://www.fhsdschools.org/about/strategic-plan 2- We celebrated the completion of a number of building projects including the FHC and FHHS auditorium. 3- We shared a monthly finance update that again identified the negative impact of Senate Bill 3 if voters approve it in April. It would create a $4 million loss in FHSD revenue in year one and $20 million loss in revenue in year five. 4- We approved a policy increasing the time for extended patron comments and discussed a policy about board code of ethics. 5- At the end, there was a brief conversation about book content. There are different interpretations about what first amendment includes. This debate plays out in hundreds of courtrooms due to the gray areas. There can be debate whether a certain word should have been allowed to be read from a book during the board comments, even if the context was to highlight its offensiveness. While gray areas exist, here are a couple points of clarity. A - I missed an opportunity to address the word that was said. While context matters, that word has caused so much harm that I needed to name the impact of the example regardless of the intent of the example. B - Different opinions on books or others topics are normal. Whether it’s from a parent or a board member, we make a space for opinions to be heard. AND C - The Board will have clearer parameters going forward that both allow for free speech and better understands what free speech looks like in this context. Francis Howell is not unique. These conversations and debates are happening all over the place. I commit to being better prepared to handle them if they reappear in the December meeting. | 8CFAbWvoG.com

entities.author: Rebecca Becky
entities.text: I’m very curious about the books in question so if someone wants to send me a message please do so. Also as a testament to 6 I would like to chime in on the great value of PAT and early childhood special education. When my son was 13 months old I noticed delays. So I called our parent educator who did an evaluation. This triggered additional evaluations through First Steps. He qualified for developmental, speech, occupational, and physical therapy. One hour of each, every week. At 3 he qualified for 4 half days of preschool where he largely spent in therapy. As he continued his education his therapies waned and now he’s a college freshman. He entered college with over 20 college credits earned while taking AP exams. He would absolutely not be where he is today without the therapists who supported him in his early education days. I am incredibly thankful for the tax dollars which support these programs because without them we wouldn’t have been able to afford any of it.

entities.author: Steven Blair For Francis Howell School Board
entities.text: Some updates from last night’s October Board Meeting. 1- Interim Superintendent Mark Delaney reiterated the district’s strong denouncement of the racist and sexually violent graffiti created by a custodian who has since been charged with a felony and fired. I restated that the decision to fire this employee was a unanimous Board decision. 2- We received a wonderful, emotionally powerful spotlight on the great work happening at Francis Howell Union High School. Their mascot is the Phoenix, illustrating how their students rise from a difficult time to flourish. 3- We received our first quarterly update on our five year Strategic Plan sharing what steps are already in motion. 4- We approved a contract allowing us to place a SRO at another elementary school. Even though the budget was approved for every school to have a SRO in June, contracts with municipalities still needed to be negotiated. 5 - We heard more about how Senate Bill 3 would remove $4 million of tax revenue immediately and will remove $20 million annually after five years. SB3 is currently on the April 2026 Ballot, but hopefully a recently filed lawsuit blocks SB3. 6- We learned more about Parents as Teachers, Early Childhood Special Education, and our Half-Day & Full Day Tuition Preschools. 7- We heard a presentation about our tax rate and different ‘no tax increase’ options. 8- We celebrated that the action of the Board last year led to paying off $13M of debt early, resulting in saving the district $4M of interest payments. 9- During Board comments, one Board member shared concerns about two books in high school libraries. Another Board member mentioned reading one of the two books and landed on a different interpretation of the book’s appropriateness. You can watch the full meeting here. https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=87RWjC6U6Fw... Thank you for staying engaged with all the great things happening at Francis Howell.

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | Preview for This Thursday’s Board Meeting. You can find the agenda here: https://go.boarddocs.com/mo/fhsdmo/Board.nsf/Public 1- Strategic Plan Update. This will be our first quarterly update of the work that is happening. These are our 2030 Goals and I am excited to hear district plans on how we will get there. See the update here: https://go.boarddocs.com/mo/fhsdmo/Board.nsf/files/DMBTDG76DC73/$file/FHSD%202030%20Quarterly%20Strategic%20Plan%20Update%20for%20BOE.pdf Our Four Pillars of Focus are Teaching & Learning, People & Workforce, Finance & Operations, and Safety & Security. 2- SRO - You will see a contract to add a SRO (School Resource Officer) at an elementary school. The money was budgeted in June, but negotiations with police departments are also required. 3 - Policy - There are 14 policies presented for second read and vote. These are mandatory updates that largely make small changes to policy to better align with new laws and procedures. 4- Senate Bill 3 Update - SB3 is still on the April 2025 Agenda. We will share again how this would defund FHSD by $4 million and grow to $20 million in lost revenue in five years. It also defunds fire stations, ambulance districts, and libraries. 5- Debt Service Levy Presentation - Most tax dollars either enter the district’s left pocket for Operations. Some enter the district’s right pocket to pay Debt. Piper Sandler will share analysis on whether we have the right amount of tax revenue entering our left pocket and right pocket or if there is an opportunity to direct some of our right pocket money into our left pocket to use for operational expenses. This would happen without any tax increase. I hope the left pocket-right pocket image made this clearer. Remember you can attend in person, watch online, and you can sign up to share your opinions in patron comments. Thank you everyone for caring for our school district and students. | dhi6xsFKe.com

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | Update from the September Meeting. 1. Tax Rates Lowering. A combination of increased valuation of real estate property and state laws connected to the Hancock Amendment will lower taxes by $0.11. This tax decrease is mandated by the state formula. 2. Facility Master Plan and Demographic Study. We learned that the number of students will likely stay flat over the next ten years, while the population will continue to grow. This is due to the age of residents and declining birth rates. The population density will change in some areas leading to an impact on school capacity. There will be a special open workshop in November where the Board will discuss the findings regarding the population shift and building capacity. I will share the meeting details once they are finalized. 3. Student Test Scores. We saw that FHSD consistently scores much higher than the rest of Missouri in Math, Language Arts, Science, and Social Studies. We also noted that the scores for ‘student groups’ are significantly lower. ‘Student groups’ refer to students who are Black, Hispanic, Free and Reduced Lunch, English as Second Language, or have a Disability. We will hear a proposed plan at the October Board Meeting regarding how we can improve our education of all students, including the student groups. 4. Senate Bill 3. We saw again how Senate Bill 3 would damage our district leading to an immediate $4 million loss tha will increase to a $20 million loss in five years. The district can only inform but board members can advocate against a ballot initiative. Thanks for staying up to date about the great things happening in Francis Howell. Thanks for your patience as this meeting update came out much later than normal. | GDU5dKV.com

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | Here’s a link to Thursday’s Agenda and a couple of highlights. 1. Academic Annual Report You will see that Francis Howell continues to outperform the rest of Missouri as one of the top districts in the state. You will also see the scores for ‘student groups’ at FHSD as generally lower. A ‘student group’ refers to low income students, English learners, black students, students with disabilities, and Hispanic students. Improving the education for each student is priority one for the districts and appears as Pillar 1 in our five year strategic plan. The whole district is stacking hands on this priority. This includes giving attention to improve any gaps. While these gaps reflect larger factors that impact other school districts and other industries, Francis Howell is responsible for addressing the needs of its students. We will hear some preliminary plans on improvements at the September and October meetings. 2. Facility Master Plan/ Demographic There is a fifty slide presentation by Hollis+Miller revealing the results of their study. I recommend you look at their projections for the next ten years. 3. Senate Bill 3 Senate Bill 3 might appear on our April Ballot depending on whether it is ruled as constitutional. Like previous months’ meetings, you will find information on how SB3 would impact our budget by largely freezing revenue income from property taxes while regular costs would continue to increase. The impact would be an estimated $4 million loss to the budget in year one and a possible $20 million budget loss in five years. More on that, later. https://go.boarddocs.com/mo/fhsdmo/Board.nsf/Public | kzH7iggl.com

entities.author: Sherry McNail
entities.text: To Jamie, Anita, Ewan, Willow and anyone else who has the same question: “Why are we so invested in this? There’s violence happening all across our country. Violence is tragic everywhere and every life taken is a child of God who deserves our love and respect and dignity. This is certainly about the tragic death, assassination, political assassination of Charlie Kirk, but it is also much bigger than an attack on an individual. It is an attack on all of us, it is an attack on the American experiment. It is an attack on our ideals. This cuts to the very foundation of who we are, of who we have been and we could be in better times. Political violence is different than any other type of violence for lots of different reasons. One because in the very act that Charlie championed of expression, that freedom of expression that is enshrined in our founding documents, and in having his life taken in that very act makes it more difficult for people to feel like they can share their ideas, that they can speak freely. We will never be able to solve all the other problems, including the violence problems that people are worried about, if we can’t have a clash of ideas safely and securely, even, especially, especially, those ideas with which you disagree. That’s why this matters so much.” - Governor Cox

entities.text: I was a teacher in upstate NY .. many of our parents worked in NYC. It was a very terrifying and surreal time. Worrying about our students and their families. Worrying about our country. Wondering if all of the acts were done yet. It was awful. But it was also beautiful seeing our country coming together, unifying, what a wonderful juxtapose.

entities.author: Jarrett Pillsbury
entities.text: Top fanCindy Powell I'm one of his supporters and I understood as well. With Evergreen happening within the same few hours, I think people calling out the omission makes sense as they weren't days or weeks apart and emotions were certainly not in short supply. And yes, it did take guts. I know Steven has the heart of a true servant leader, he stumbles, he falls, he gets up again and I truly believe tries to do his level best. Oh and he's not a perfect person either. On today of all days, we need to realize how much more we ALL have in common than what sets us apart. Thank you, President Blair, and appreciate your further comments. The loss of life is a terrible thing and thank you for the statement.

entities.author: Ewan Ross
entities.text: I remember vividly being woken up by my younger brother telling me a plane had crashed in New York. Even more vividly sitting and watching the 2nd plane appear in shot during the live news coverage. Even 3,300 miles away the shock of seeing that precise moment haunts the mind to this day. I flew over NY later that year, the pilot pointed out ground zero - seeing the scale of the site from the sky was another gut punch.

entities.author: Ewan Ross
entities.text: I totally get where you are coming from on this.School shootings, while rare, are now so much of American culture (ask a non national about America, they won’t talk about freedom, wealth, the American Dream - they’ll talk about school shootings though) and so it would be an endless task to bring up each one 140-170 per year, certainly more than two a week.Kirk’s shooting, the motives behind which aren’t clear yet, but are most likely due to his dangerous and harmful perspectives, represents something a bit different (although I don’t recall posts about the 4 political shootings in MN which resulted in two deaths and two hospitalizations) - different enough to make the national news cycles etc.I would point out, given that you raise SROs and your silly armed admin - Kirk was literally surrounded by law enforcement and guns. The assassin is still at large. They did no good because they do no good. They are, in fact, part of the problem (guns being present and considered a viable solution to anything) while you try to bring community together and decry violence do some introspection on your own, now personal, role in perpetuating the very culture that leads us both to Kirk and to school shootings.

entities.author: Steven Blair For Francis Howell School Board
entities.text: Jamie Carlsen Martin Thank you for the kind words. I disagree with a lot of what Charlie Kirk says AND I am concerned with political violence. I am afraid that this moment can lead to more violence against others if we don’t take the lead in how we treat and talk about others. You and everyone around are the center of my heart. I want your safety. I want the same safety for people in Francis Howell Families. I want FHEA’s safety. I want the Board’s, admin’s, and teachers’ safety. And, I definitely want students’ safety. Political violence that kills or harms someone we disagree with doesn’t just stay with adults. Leadership creates culture and I am trying to create a culture where every life is seen as filled with immeasurable worth and feels safety because of it. That basis allows us to do a lot of good. I appreciate you and know your heart, as well. Thank you for listening!!

entities.text: Willow Wideman Hello Willow. You’re right. I could have added the victims at Evergreen High School to my post. My intent was to present a different message than the ones I have been hearing today which could lead to more violence. I am committed to the safety of kids and teens. I have approved a budget that funds SRO’s at each school and approved a full time Director of Safety and Security to help us provide a safe environment for students and staff as well. People’s safety matters a lot to me, especially kids because each life is filled with immeasurable value.

entities.author: Steven Blair For Francis Howell School Board
entities.text: First- The comments expressed herein are my own comments as a private citizen and are not made on behalf of the Francis Howell School District. —— Today Charlie Kirk was killed at one of his college debating events. Violence has no place in politics, or any other sphere in our lives. We can argue, protest, and campaign but violence to one damages all people. A human life is a human life, filled with immeasurable worth. I am committed to a culture where we can challenge opinions and tell someone ‘You’re wrong’ without demeaning the person. We all make the culture that we live in and I choose Love: Love in the goal for all people and Love in the path. I have tried to display this and will look in the mirror to find ways I can improve. Thank you everyone for your commitment to build #OneHowell together in all our actions.

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | I would like to honor Betty Honey, mother of our board member, Carolie Owens. Betty passed away on August 29th, 2025 at the age of 100. She taught public school for 32 years, including being selected an Outstanding Elementary Teacher in America in 1973. Betty proudly taught in one of the first integrated classrooms in the US. Betty lived a full life impacting countless students through the amazing, sacred profession of being a public school teacher. While Betty passed away at the age of 100, it is never easy to say goodbye to one’s mom. I ask for prayers, kind thoughts, warm wishes, etc. towards Carolie Owens. Carolie, I see the very best of Betty in you. We are all fortunate to have you extending Betty’s legacy and serving the students at Francis Howell. Reach Carolie at Carolie Owens for Francis Howell or Carolie.owens@fhsdschools.org. | HcVQD5I.com

entities.authorKey: name:steven blair for francis howell school board
entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | The Board of Education met last night for our monthly meeting. While there weren’t any substantial votes at the meeting, there were some highlights. 1- We had two students from Independence Elementary lead the Pledge of Allegiance. This is a new practice that we will continue throughout the school year. 2- We had great news about the FHN Odor Update. There are signs that SM Wilson has both identified the problem and found a solution that is already working. 3- We received an extensive update about all the construction projects happening around the District including HVAC updates, FHHS wrestling room and auditorium, FHC auditorium, Henderson addition, HVAC, and new gym, Fairmount addition and parking, and more. 4- We learned more about Senate Bill 3. There will be lawsuits challenging its constitutionality. If it makes it to the ballot, the entire county would vote on it. Briefly, Senate Bill 3 would freeze property taxes while all district costs would grow with regular inflation. Francis Howell receives around 75% of its budget from residential property taxes. If Senate Bill 3 passes, the fiscal damage would grow each year as the gap between our frozen revenue stream and inflated costs would grow. We will continue to provide information updates. 5. Lastly, during Board comments I shared a brief comment about the Mike Dominguez settlement. I shared that I/We cannot share any more, but I/We can listen all we want. You and your opinions matter. You can email me at steven.blair@fhsdschools.org and I will be glad to listen to your concerns on this matter, or any other. The very best days for Francis Howell are ahead of us. I’m excited about this school year and everything good that will happen in each of our 23 campuses for our nearly 17000 students. Thank you. | vqt7V.com

entities.text: Jane Yager conversely my 3rd is a year or so out from starting and while the politics at the top can be a tad absurd the district itself has been nothing but superb - one reason I’m willing to step up and shout a lot about doing right by the district - because the actions of a board may take years to have an actual impact and I want my smallest to have the same experience my high schooler had, which has been, almost exclusively, superb,While losing 0.1% of the annual budget to what appears to be a con man does, indeed, suck - the weirdness of the last 2 and a bit years should be behind us (and caused this) and while the model of having citizens run a school board is always going to produce weird results and missteps (amateurs running a $250M organization makes no sense, but we must pick the best we can) it is what we are saddled with as a state/nation.

entities.author: Gary Bledsoe
entities.text: Mr. Blair, I understand that you have been put in an awkward position with this issue. As a long time taxpayer and patron of FHSD, I am very concerned about how the district has handled this issue. It seems to me that leaving two critical positions open to cover the cost of a very serious mistake in the contract structure that a person to could be paid a substantial benefit for absolutely no work. We need answers as to:1. Who vetted this person?2. Was it his choice to leave?3. If it was his choice, who was responsible for not including a contract clause protecting the district from that type of action?4. In any case, what actions are being formulated to prevent future issues like this happening again! Going forward, the board needs to be more transparent when these issues arise. They also need to be more transparent in how they are working to prevent these type issues from happening in the first place.Robbing Peter to pay Paul, which is basically how leaving two critical positions open to pay for this “mistake”, you plan to stay on budget, is not a solution but a deflection from a larger problem which is accountability. The students and taxpayers in FHSD deserve better.Respectfully,William Bledsoe

Until these rogue school boards are forced to be transparent with taxpayers and THEIR money, you can expect more of this!!!!

entities.text: Steven Blair For Francis Howell School Board I’m aware how budgets work Steven.If I’m budgeting for my home I don’t not pay for something simply because it wasn’t budgeted if that thing is both vital and will cost me more in the long run.I’m also aware that a $250M budget for a school district which has numerous financing options and reserve cash is completely and utterly not comparible to a home. (For reference if I had a $40,000 budget for my home this would be like foregoing a $40 charge for home repairs, rather than say $40 on eating out)

entities.author: Ewan Ross
entities.text: Jeff Snodgrass without knowing the story how would that be appropriate?Here’s what is most likely, given all the circumstances -Something was uncovered, after he was hired, that made it clear he was unsuitable for the job but was not something he could be fired for cause over.At which point the options are - pay off his whole contract, keep him, or negotiate.Would we, as voters, be happier with a $750k payout if we could know what went on? (I would be, actually, if the truth was out and every other school district in the land had this information readily available to avoid the same mistake)Or with a superintendent not fit for the job? (To me this is the option that should see anyone voting for immediately resign)I feel a lot of folks, however, likely a majority, would prefer the minimum payout, even if that means Dominguez gets to enforce silence.I’m gonna remain mad at everyone who, against advice of sensible folks, rushed the process - Steven did back this rushed process, so yeah, that’s a big black mark. Enough to resign over? Not hardly. It’s not like he spent $3000 without any approval to advance his own agenda.

entities.author: Erin Shetler
entities.text: While I appreciate the information, I think it’s important to note that eliminating admin roles does impact students in the classroom. Implying otherwise devalues those roles and is not correct. I know we want cuts to stay as far away from classroom impact as possible, but language matters, especially for the future of these roles. The people in these roles presumably provided support and resources to teachers and students. This might allow us to stay within our budget, but that’s not the same thing as not having an impact on learning.

entities.author: Steven Blair For Francis Howell School Board
entities.text: Jennifer Dettwiler Hello Jennifer. You are right. Not filling positions is not a long term solution and not what we had in mind when we passed the balanced budget in June. For this year, this does allow us to keep a balanced budget which is very important to the community and to the Board. Personnel decisions always have a piece of confidentiality to them. However, we are committed to being as transparent as possible according to the law. Keep asking questions and sharing concerns. We are listening. Thank you!

entities.text: Mr Blair previously shared the exact language in the severance agreement that prevents the board from commenting on the reasons behind the separation. We can ask all we want, but if they answer the district will end up in court and it will cost a lot more. Maybe some of the reporters digging into it will turn up factual information, but anything being said right now is just speculation. Given that the agreement was approved unanimously by seven people with very different viewpoints and all thought this was the best of the options in front of them, I imagine the alternatives must have been really awful.Thank you to Mr. Delaney and others who are stepping up for a very challenging year while we wait for the next budget to allow hiring again.
