entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | (Also shared via District email) FHSD Community: My name is Steven Blair and I serve as President of the Francis Howell School Board. I am thrilled to announce that the Board took action on Sunday evening to name Mr. Mark Delaney as Interim Superintendent for the remainder of the 2025-2026 school year. With 20 years of experience in Francis Howell, we are confident Mr. Delaney will provide the District with steady, capable leadership while the Board carefully considers longer-term plans for the position. On behalf of the Board, I want to publicly thank Mr. Delaney for graciously agreeing to serve as our Interim Superintendent through June 30, 2026. We ask that you give your full support to Mr. Delaney as he leads our District. The Board is committed to operating within the Board-approved balanced budget for the 2025-2026 fiscal year. Among other cost-saving opportunities, District Administration and the Board do not plan to fill the Deputy Superintendent position vacated by Mr. Delaney, or the vacant Director of Secondary Education position for this school year. Savings from these vacancies and other adjustments will allow the District to operate within a balanced budget without negatively impacting student programs and academic resources. These are two important positions and the Board recognizes this is not a sustainable long-term structure. We wish to recognize and thank those on the FHSD team who will help cover the vacancies. Their agreement to pitch in displays the #OneHowell commitment we see across our District. We are excited to welcome our students back to school next week. We are the #1 school district in St. Charles County and we do not want to stop there. More than 2,000 employees are preparing to make this a fantastic school year. Our Interim Superintendent, staff, teachers, administrative teams, paraprofessionals, nurses, counselors, bus drivers, custodians, cafeteria workers, maintenance, technicians, grounds crews and others, are all ready to provide the best education for every student entrusted to us. There are amazing stories coming from every corner of our District. There is so much to celebrate and we do not want you to miss a thing. Let’s have a great school year! Steven Blair President Francis Howell School Board | NF5pOPsb.com

entities.author: Jamie Martin
entities.text: James Zerbonia I always think it’s interesting to chalk lists like yours up to “political viewpoints”—it’s also a list of humans with unique challenges. I’m sure you don’t believe personal liberties are only applicable to people who look or love or present a certain way—most folks wouldn’t. But in 2020, that was the clash we experienced (and a clash as old as time); that is, where one person’s liberty ends and others’ begin. Examples include whether some restricted movement or temporary mask mandates might be necessary to ensure our hospital systems didn’t become overwhelmed by too many of us getting sick at once or higher rates of Black deaths at the hands of police or whether gay youth should be able to read abt gay characters or whether fear and discomfort around other people’s gender/bathroom needs should be prioritized above some folks safety and dignity.But what if the problem isn’t pendulum swings? What if the problem is a complete inability to be curious about one another, allow for differences, and navigate social change together? What if we fight a new culture war every generation or two because we haven’t learned how to hold two ideas at once—how to honor our shared interests and still make our own choices?Ultimately, my comment is factual: this backlash to social change is far more expensive/harmful than just navigating the change itself.

entities.text: If he was pursuing a job with another district prior to his contract start of July 1st I would think we could fight paying him. Whomever is drawing up these contracts needs to do a better job and put a clause in them. Hopefully this is a lesson learned. We can pay him for never starting a job however the district doesn’t put hardly any $$ towards the sports teams. Us parents have to fork over $$ to help our kids teams & raise $$ to get equipment. All while paying our higher taxes to support the district. I will think twice about voting for an increase to support the schools.

entities.author: Jamie Martin
entities.text: James Zerbonia I’m no party faithful, so you won’t see me championing one or the other “side,” but it is now well documented that this round of culture wars was launched as a high-level orchestration by partisan interest groups on the right. They aren’t shy about it. Christopher Rufo (Manhattan Institute Fellow and Heritage Foundation affiliate) declared that intent openly on multiple occasions—his speech at Hillsdale College saying we had to reach universal public school distrust, his tweet abt “brand freezing” CRT, and his later tweet saying they would do the same to LGBTQ issues…Glen Youngkin in Virginia, the state Republican Party in TX, Moms for Liberty founders—all partners in funding and messaging. Turning Point USA (National PAC) held school board election trainings to support anti-public ed board members. As an education researcher, I can tell you this culture wars, at least, was no organic pendulum swing. Millions of dollars and high-level political expertise built this moment.

entities.author: James Zerbonia
entities.text: Melanie Wilcox Renken Please tell me how the man was hired in the first place if he was the wrong person to lead our kids? What due diligence was done by the board prior where we hired a man who then due to unforeseen circumstances can’t do the job but we pay him $250k? Those of us who work in the private sector understand bad hires happen but buy outs are not usually a part of the process for a guy who did not work a day. The schools don’t have unlimited funds like a business would and can’t afford to take a $250k hit. The next conversation will be about a tax increase to absorb this and the cost of the new high school.

entities.author: Melanie Wilcox Renken
entities.text: Justin SmithTrust me—I completely agree with you that he was paid despite not having worked. But, unfortunately, I see it happen all the time. Terminating employees with employment contracts is just different from terminating at-will employees, and generally comes with a price tag. In my original post, I was simply trying to convey that I am very happy that the Board decided to get out of the contract before he could cause damage to the district. It came with a price, but I like this option better than one in which we are paying the wrong person to lead our district while he causes harm to our kids. I know Carolie Owens for Francis Howell Schools to be someone of incredible character, and who truly cares about our kids and wants what’s best for them. So if she and Sarah Oelke—both career educators—were part of a unanimous vote to terminate the contract with Dominguez, I have to trust there was good reason and that our kids are being cared for. Of course, I’d love to know what the board learned about Dominguez after the ink dried, but I know the Distrct can’t be the source of that information without having to pay even more money for breaching the separation agreement and/or subjecting the Distrct to legal action we shouldn’t be spending money on. Again—I am not against you here. And not trying to argue. To the contrary—I’m trying to give people some peace that what happened is not necessarily treacherous. Rather, there are legal reasons that justify it.

entities.author: Steven Blair For Francis Howell School Board
entities.text: Alma Gayle Hello Alma. Thank you for asking. This is the first time I have seen your name discussing Francis Howell so I want to say it’s nice to meet you. We have a legal settlement with Mike Dominguez. In it, it states Both parties agree that ifasked about the resolution of any employment dispute, they will respond, "Dr. Dominguezresigned from the Francis Howell School District effective on July 31, 2025. I cannot commentfurther on a confidential personnel matter."If we say any more, the district is at risk for more money. I am certain that the taxpayers would not want that. In a little bit, we will share a way that the district is able to save money elsewhere to either partly or entirely cover the $250,000 cost so it doesn’t impact the rest of the budget/staff/students. Please look for that announcement as well. Keep asking questions of elected officials. Keep holding us accountable. I ask that you also keep engaged when additional information does get shared that we are allowed to share. Thank you, Alma!

entities.text: Christopher Gumper Hello Christopher. I think your critique is valid. I understand that you and others want more answers right now. I would love to share more. Our separation agreement only allow board members to say the following. Both parties agree that ifasked about the resolution of any employment dispute, they will respond, "Dr. Dominguezresigned from the Francis Howell School District effective on July 31, 2025. I cannot commentfurther on a confidential personnel matter."If we say more, it could cost the district a lot of money. I know that you and others taxpayers do not want that, either. I can share that the district found a way to save money elsewhere that will either mostly, or entirely, cover the $250,000. I’ll share more about that shortly. Your concerns are good concerns. Elected officials need to be challenged and I welcome any future comment you would like to share. Thank you for caring for Francis Howell!

entities.author: Brian Gomski
entities.text: Thanks for sharing this and providing more insight.Reading between the lines, it sounds like the board MAY have learned new information that led to a change in course. If so, that makes sense and I understand there are legal limits to what can be shared.That said, even if the outcome was unavoidable, it raises a larger question about the contract structure itself. There should be language in future contracts to ensure compensation only begins once someone actually starts work—and that resigning beforehand doesn’t trigger a payout.This comment is less about this specific case and more about making sure the district is protected from needing to negotiate settlements like this in the first place.If a candidate balks at accepting an offer with a start-date contingency, or if unsettling and undisclosed information is discovered about the candidate before the start date, that is a good thing. It will help eliminate bad candidates.Appreciate your continued engagement with the community.

entities.author: Sarah Johnson
entities.text: The fact that the board, known for its division, voted unanimously on this matter should speak volumes. However, stakeholders deserve transparency and while both parties are bound by a confidentiality agreement, the vagueness leads to speculation, fingerpointing, and more division in the community. The district has struggled with an erosion of trust among the community, and some clarity about how the resignation was initiated, whether by him or the board, is needed. It is a costly mistake. One can surmise this might have been avoided by a less rushed hiring process and/or a more thorough vetting by both the search firm that presented him as a candidate and the board. Ultimately, I hope people understand that this wasn't a lightly made decision, and if every board member agreed upon it, then they must have deemed it the best option for a no-win situation.

entities.author: Melanie Wilcox Renken
entities.text: I agree that $250k is a lot of money. But the damage and cost of allowing the wrong person lead our district would have been much, much greater. Regrettable hires happen every day and to every employer. In my experience, the worst decision and employer can make is to continue allowing the wrong person to lead. I, for one, am celebrating the fact that our board came together and unanimously decided to do what they believe is best for our kids—-knowing the backlash and criticism they would face. It is not unusual or the least bit shady for employers to be prohibited from speaking about personnel decisions. I hope we will not let a disgruntled former board member make this into a controversy that it simply is not.

entities.author: Jamie Martin
entities.text: Dropping in with a few thoughts:1–We wouldn’t have needed a new super if we hadn’t run off a highly competent one, along with a whole handful of administrators and librarians.2–The votes to hire and to separate were unanimous. When folks who agree on very little can agree on their only employer, it says something.3–It’s hard to attract quality candidates when your district’s in the throes of the culture wars, and your board keeps trying to insert party agendas. Maybe now we’ll have more to choose from.4–If we take the time needed to put the candidate in front of the community and have more interaction before a hire (as Harry said), perhaps this situation could be prevented.5–All of the above are directly traced back to a board that focused more on books and gender than stewardship of public education.6–Let us remember Wentzville and be grateful Roumpos found a different district rather than naming a toxic work environment to the tune of $1 million.Culture wars sure are expensive.

entities.author: Steven Blair For Francis Howell School Board
entities.text: I understand that a short, ambiguous statement produces a lot of questions. I have read a lot of great questions in the comments. Thank you. Your questions show that you care about this district, its staff, and especially its students. A sunshine request produced information that is available to the public. It includes information on the settlement and what we can say. The settlement was for one year of salary ($250,000) out of the three year $750,000 contract. It also reveals that the vote to accept this settlement was 7-0. We are legally limited to what we can say. I will share what I can. I will treat every request for more information as a valid request by a staff/parent/community member who cares. This is obviously not the conclusion we hoped for when we hired Dr. Dominguez. The Board will discuss options regarding the superintendent position, shortly. I can say that the entire Board is thrilled to have Mark Delaney serve as our Interim Superintendent. We are thankful for his work and the rest of the administrative team’s work to get us ready for the school year. Soon, we will have teachers, staff, and students filling our buildings in the best school district in St. Charles County. The Board will be ready to do what we can to help provide the best education for all students. Thank you, everyone. Your interest in all the workings of the district reveal your love for Francis Howell and we’re a better district for it.

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | Attention - The below was just emailed to Francis Howell parents and staff. I am including it here to inform the larger community. Thank you. FHSD Community: In June, we shared that Dr. Mike Dominguez would not be able to begin his duties as Superintendent on July 1 due to unforeseen circumstances. The purpose of this communication is to provide you with an update. The Francis Howell School District and Dr. Dominguez announce that he has resigned effective July 31, 2025 to allow him to pursue opportunities that better align with the current needs of his family. Deputy Superintendent Mark Delaney will continue to serve as Interim Superintendent. As a long-time Francis Howell educator, Mr. Delaney has the right combination of experience and relational abilities necessary to lead the District, and the Board is grateful for his willingness to serve in this important leadership capacity. I want you to know that the Board and District leaders are laser-focused on our mission and our new strategic plan. With a strong foundation and clear roadmap in place, we are positioned to make steady progress on our ambitious goals. Francis Howell has a rich legacy of academic excellence and I have every confidence that the dedicated teachers, staff and administrators will ensure our District continues to excel for years to come. We look forward to welcoming back students and the remainder of our teachers and staff in just a few short weeks! Steven Blair President Francis Howell Board of Education | Y6MNe.com

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | Hello I am sharing the district-wide email to everyone that was just sent to parents and staff. ————————- FHSD Community: Summer is in full swing and we hope that our students and staff are finding time to relax and recharge. We are reaching out today to share an important leadership update with our community. Due to unforeseen circumstances, Dr. Mike Dominguez is unfortunately unable to begin his duties as Superintendent on July 1. The FHSD Board of Education has appointed Deputy Superintendent Mr. Mark Delaney to act as Interim Superintendent until Dr. Dominguez is able to start. We are all diligently preparing for the start of the next school year and look forward to seeing everyone back on our campuses in August! Thank you, FHSD Communications | UNI9ru.com

entities.text: disappointing Watching the meeting I wanted to make a quick comment on the book discussion - the 'algorithm' Jane is talking about is most likely just a vlookup in excel against a list of books. The accusation that librarians cannot do their job because she and the last board increased their workload with makework to assuage hyper conservative nonsense is a silly one - knwoing what is in the libraries and vetting it upon entry is the bulk of their job and something they already do. The additional work was the issue. Someone should have pointed that out to her. We already know that FHFamilies and various followers of theirs rely on online curated lists of books to get faux upset about (faux upset because they have not challenged these books) - it would be easy, and essentially free, to create an excel sheet (or google docs or what have you) with a list of all material in FHSD, and a list of books you might find inappropriate and simply add =VLOOKUP(A2,Range:Range,1,FALSE) and then say "I found books that conservative book banners would not like" I will do this for the district for $1 if you so wish, although even that would be a pointless waste of money because we already pay our library staff and teachers to do this, and they're great at it. (Jane is basically bringing in a hyper conservative shuckster who is bafflign her with the word algorithm and a promise to push her agenda, because hey, free money pulled from education is a hyper conservative wet dream)

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | Update from Board Meeting 1- We approved the 25-26 Balanced Budget. 2- We approved Policy 6310 - This adds Efficiency to the Transparency in 6310 allowing librarians more time with students. 3- Third Party Book Review - We discussed a third party company to review incoming books. Concerns about the company’s background were shared. No vote occurred. 4- Full time School Resource Officers will be stationed at every school in 25-26. 5- School Protection Officer - We voted to allow this designation to only our incoming Safety and Security Director 6- We received a report on the Francis Howell North smell from SM Wilson Co. They shared additional smoke tests, fixes, and upcoming fixes they believe will solve the problem. 7- We celebrated our CFO Carol Embree as she retired on June 30. 8- We celebrated our Superintendent Ken Roumpos who will become the Kirkwood Superintendent on July 1. 9- We named that the Board will discuss the Resolution Against Racism at our summer ‘retreat’ meeting. Date TBA 10- We finished the Board Meeting before 8:30pm!!!!! | 8RgYYV8wN.com

entities.author: Ewan Ross
entities.text: I took a few moments to rewrite the section of policy to meet a more sensible threshold and to avoid discrimination based on position - arguably if SPOs are an improvement to safety then a para or a member of the dining staff are better placed to be of use assuming they meet the training requirements. This basically takes the redline policy proposed and makes it neat.School Protection Officers Notwithstanding provisions to the contrary in this Policy, the District may designate one or more members of staff as a school protection officers in accordance with section 160.665 of the Revised Statutes of Missouri. School protection officers are authorized to carry a concealed firearm or self-defense spray device if approved by the Board. Prior to designating such officers, the Board will conduct a public hearing on the initiation of such Program. Notice must be given in a publication of general circulation in the city or court in which the District is located at least fifteen (15) days before the hearing.However, in order to protect personal information of an employee, the Board may meet in closed session to determine whether to allow the designation of a school protection officer for an individual employee and to determine whether to allow the employee to carry a concealed firearm or self-defense spray device as a school protection officer and to protect the School Protection Officer’s identity. Those seeking to be designated as a school protection officer must make a written request to the Superintendent along with proof of ownership of a valid concealed carry endorsement or permit, plus documentation demonstrating a need to carry. This will take the form of a written submission from the applicant and may be supplemented with endorsements or references from individuals who can supply evidence that such a need exists.Need to carryAny applicant must demonstrate a need, not simply a desire, to carry a concealed firearm or self-defense spray. They must demonstrate that in the execution of their duties it can be reasonably expected that they would encounter a situation where a concealed firearm or self-defense spray would be reasonably expected to improve safety outcomes for students, staff and patrons of the district. This need must be demonstrated to be expected to occur at least once within any three year period based on the current district’s history of incidents along with a statistical outlook of such incidents for a district of the size, demographics and wealth of the Francis Howell School District.Closed session meeting to determine allowing an employee to concealed carryPrior to holding a closed session to determine the carrying of a concealed firearm or self defense spray the board will give notice to the public of the timing of the meeting, and provide, with identity redacted, all submissions made to establish need. Notice must be given in a publication of general circulation in the city or court in which the District is located at least fifteen (15) days before the meeting.Given the gravity of such an allowance approval of the request will require a 75% or greater ‘yes’ vote from the board based on total number of board members currently elected to serve the district. All teachers and administrators seeking designation as a school protection officer shall also submit a certificate of school protection officer training program completed from a training program approved by the Director of Public Safety.If the District designates a school protection officer, the District must notify the Director of Public Safety of: 1. Full name, date of birth and address of the officer; 2. The name of the school district; and 3. The date such person was designated as a school protection officer. Such identity information will not be considered public information under the State’s Sunshine Law.Such school protection officers will not be permitted to allow any firearm or device out of their personal control, while the firearm or device is on school property. Violation of this provision will subject the offending officer to termination proceedings.Such school protection officers will take every precaution to avoid accidental discharge of their firearm or device. Violation of this provision will subject the offending officer to termination proceedings.Such school protection officers will only draw their firearm or device when circumstances dictate it is the only option. Violation of this provision will subject the offending officer to termination proceedings.

Those seeking to be designated as a school protection officer must make a written request to the Superintendent along with proof of ownership of a valid concealed carry endorsement or permit, plus documentation demonstrating a need to carry. This will take the form of a written submission from the applicant and may be supplemented with endorsements or references from individuals who can supply evidence that such a need exists.Need to carryAny applicant must demonstrate a need, not simply a desire, to carry a concealed firearm or self-defense spray. They must demonstrate that in the execution of their duties it can be reasonably expected that they would encounter a situation where a concealed firearm or self-defense spray would be reasonably expected to improve safety outcomes for students, staff and patrons of the district. This need must be demonstrated to be expected to occur at least once within any three year period based on the current district’s history of incidents along with a statistical outlook of such incidents for a district of the size, demographics and wealth of the Francis Howell School District.Closed session meeting to determine allowing an employee to concealed carryPrior to holding a closed session to determine the carrying of a concealed firearm or self defense spray the board will give notice to the public of the timing of the meeting, and provide, with identity redacted, all submissions made to establish need. Notice must be given in a publication of general circulation in the city or court in which the District is located at least fifteen (15) days before the meeting.Given the gravity of such an allowance approval of the request will require a 75% or greater ‘yes’ vote from the board based on total number of board members currently elected to serve the district. All teachers and administrators seeking designation as a school protection officer shall also submit a certificate of school protection officer training program completed from a training program approved by the Director of Public Safety.If the District designates a school protection officer, the District must notify the Director of Public Safety of: 1. Full name, date of birth and address of the officer; 2. The name of the school district; and 3. The date such person was designated as a school protection officer. Such identity information will not be considered public information under the State’s Sunshine Law.Such school protection officers will not be permitted to allow any firearm or device out of their personal control, while the firearm or device is on school property. Violation of this provision will subject the offending officer to termination proceedings.Such school protection officers will take every precaution to avoid accidental discharge of their firearm or device. Violation of this provision will subject the offending officer to termination proceedings.Such school protection officers will only draw their firearm or device when circumstances dictate it is the only option. Violation of this provision will subject the offending officer to termination proceedings.

entities.author: Ewan Ross
entities.text: If 5 is simply establishing a framework rather than actually approving (as it appears after a little thought and conversation) then I do not think policy should be built to set up one individual to be armed.A more generic policy would do, but it should contain verbiage that when applying to be an SPO any individual in the district must meet mandated training requirements (per law, and preferably beyond what the law expects and up to that which is expected of SROs) and, and this is the most important part for me, must establish a need to carry, rather than simply a desire. A tangible requirement of the job which means they need to be armed. Not the boogeyman of a “what if” as that opens too many doors, but an actual demonstrated need that will come up in a reasonable timeframe (say in a given 2 year period)As intimated to the board in prior emails my job has similar requirements around data access - if you cannot demonstrate a need to have access to a source of data then you do not get that access regardless of if you think maybe possibly it might be helpful one day, or your direct reports have that access etc.Such a policy makes sense. If we lived in a world where a job existed such that there was an actual demonstrated need for someone to carry a gun in the district then I don’t think anyone would oppose that, even someone as opposed to firearms as myself, I equally cannot see why anyone would desire an employee to be armed if they could not demonstrate a need.

entities.author: Jennifer Main
entities.text: #5 - Something else to consider. I agree with many other points made here and elsewhere regarding doubts about whether this individual having a weapon will actually add to student and staff safety, and that should be our number one priority. However, have we considered the safety of this individual while he has a firearm? If he were to be on-site at a building during an incident that involved outside law enforcement, could they easily identify him as district staff and not the perpetrator of violence if he has a weapon out?

entities.author: Meghan Guilford
entities.text: Steven Blair For Francis Howell School Board I noticed this at the June 6 meeting. The SPO is a designation and not the Director of Saftey and Security hire and doesn’t have to be a Law Enforcement officer. It’s a new term and the DSS and SPO are not interchangeable. During discussions it was stumbled over with the terms and person. SPO is *only* an acronym for School Protection Officer who has taken the course and the School Board has approved to carry on school grounds. Are you saying the DSS is a current LEO? That seems inaccurate like he’s holding two jobs. A current LEO would be on a police entities payroll. I thought he was a former LEO? I don’t discredit this DSS’ ability to handle a gun in a stressful situation. But I do not agree that another gun is needed in the schools.

entities.author: Ewan Ross
entities.text: Steven Blair For Francis Howell School Board it isn’t similar at all.First up it is questionable that the presence of a firearm is helpful (no evidence suggests it is, and research on the matter suggests that the presence of firearms increases rather than decreases the number of fatalities should a shooting occur (largely because shooters are aware of the presence and thus come prepared)So essentially you are adding nothing, it is security theater and machismo. Nothing more.He isn’t an active law enforcement officer right? To be a law enforcement officer one has to actually be employed in law enforcement. He isn’t employed in law enforcement, he is a director of safety and security. The fact he wants to concealed carry carry is a big huge red flag. If he wants to be a cop he should be a cop.In terms of added protection - school shootings are vanishingly rare albeit high impact headline news. The chances of one occurring are essentially negligible at any given school.Let’s say, in a 10 year period, one active shooter incident occurred in the district (which seems an overestimate given that there hasn’t been a shooting in the school in the past 20 years, meaning guns in schools, had they been there, would have had zero protective value for 20 years) - we have 23 campuses in the district, meaning if the SPO was present only at schools for his entire working day - the chances of him being present during such an event are a little under 5%, given that there is no way he is spending all his time at schools these chances are likely less than 1%, and given that an armed officer on scene being actually helpful in a shooting is not a certainty you’re sub 1% in terms of being actually helpful once a decade.On top of which presumably SROs carry other equipment (cuffs, body armor, other non lethal protective measures) making them a better fit than some dude in a suit with a John Wayne complex and a yearning for his youth to be actually helpful once a decade in such an event.The teachers notably also don’t appear to want this, so let’s stick to our guns (haha) and demonstrate that we are for the teachers, and data driven, rather than carrying on with this utter nonsensical approach.

entities.author: Steven Blair For Francis Howell School Board
entities.text: Meghan Guilford Thank you Meghan. I understand the questions. Having any employee with a weapon in our schools can be a cause for concern. We have decided that having a police officer as a SRO at each school with a weapon is helpful for safety and security. Having another law enforcement officer conceal and carry is similar to adding to the SRO type safety. If a threat happens at a school where he is visiting, there will be two armed officers to protect our kids. I have zero interest in arming teachers, etc. I see his status as an active law enforcement officer and the conceal and carry aspect as key distinctions about this one case.

entities.author: Meghan Guilford
entities.text: Steven Blair For Francis Howell School Board I have major concerns that our district does not have the money to pay for this service. And disagree that the service is needed. a) There is a Challenge Book procedure in place (that the last Board created). How many times has this been utilized? (It's <10 I believe). Shouldn't the district have a full list of books in each school library? If they are concerned about personal teacher libraries - hire a Para or secure a volunteer to catalogue the list. Students need volunteer hours for our NHS. There is an App that can scan the barcode and create the list. It's not difficult. b) The "Book Issue" isn't as big of deal as much as it keeps getting brought up. Certain individuals or PACs are holding onto this and no longer focusing on the real issues our students face everyday in our schools. If the Challenge Book Procedure was having to see (and agree with) 5+ Books a Month/school or 100s a month over the entire district, then it would be an issue. There is a procedure - let's start there. c) It was discussed in the 6/5 Meeting that a Para for each Elementary Library would be helpful for creating book lists and helping the librarians with shelving books. Hiring Paras would be a better use of money than hiring an outside company. **We shouldn't waste money on a non-issue.**

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | Board Meeting Preview. Here are a few key items for the June 19th meeting. 1-Approving the 25-26 Balanced Budget. Our CFO shared a longer presentation about the budget proposal on June 5th, but we will vote to approve or amend it at this meeting. State law requires the Board to approve a budget before July 1. 2- Policy 6310 - Librarians discussed possible changes to keep the Transparency of 6310 but add some ways to be more Efficient. We had a first reading of the policy changes at the June 5th Meeting and will vote on 6310 tomorrow, June 19. 3- Third Party Book Review - A Board member requested that we discuss a company coming to share their opinion about all the books in our libraries. This will be a discussion item but there will not be a vote to adopt/hire. 4- Student Resource Officers - The 25-26 budget includes adding a full time Student Resource Officer at the last schools that needed one. Part of the agenda also includes contract language with the municipalities associated with each of those schools. 5- Student Protection Officer. This is a new title according to Missouri Statute. The Board will discuss a revised Policy 1432 which clearly designates that this title exclusively refers to our new Director of Safety and Security, who is a current law enforcement officer. This person and ONLY this person, will be designated as a SPO and allowed to conceal and carry while he is visiting schools to make sure they are as safe as possible. Any other person would have to receive their own approval. 6- This will be the last meeting for our Superintendent Ken Roumpos and our CFO Carol Embree. Our district is better because of both of their leadership. I will share an update after the meeting to help everyone stay informed. Thank you. | TRKvi.com

entities.author: Becky Hormuth
entities.text: Steven Blair For Francis Howell School Board well the narrative sure sounded like it to me as an observer! IMO you can paint it however, but I oppose the idea! Second point, I would like more of an outlined plan of specifics…the extra duties the instructional coaches are expected of. Like I said, I am familiar with the role. In addition, I also saw groups of students that I intervened with, which no longer is happening. All role requires additional at times. Some expected, some personal driven. Director Oleke asked what the stipend is for, and it was answered by a generalized statement given by Ms. Simpkins. Out of fairness it was not clear. Can you tell me specifically the additional work responsibilities they are assigned outside of the work day that they haven’t already been doing? Personally, I will now be scaling back tremendously next year and not be participating in an additional building committees or extracurriculars not mandated in my contract. As much as I’m not a fan of it, I’ve always been very involved, but I’m out of giving. Since I don’t get a stipend for work beyond the work day, I will also (as difficult & stressful as it will be) end my day at contract time, not answer late night parent emails, along with having to limit all the best practice actions I continuously do on a daily basis after work hours.

entities.author: Ewan Ross
entities.text: To put it in a context that makes sense to me, and perhaps other that work in corporate America….In my role I have reasonably wide access to all manner of data, including data classified as secret or some other level of company confidential (ie proprietary- nothing like government secrets, but information that if competitors got hold of it could be harmful to the business in terms of giving away strategy, technologies etc). Our organization operates under a “need to know” basis for all data, therefore it is wholly plausible that I have access to information that my boss is not privy to - his role does not need to know the specifics of data I am working on - he supervises a group all of whom have different needs to know based on their projects.He is not a front line worker in the space, thus regardless of how much the business trusts him he does not get access to tools (databases, APIs, documents) which could be of danger to the company.Likewise without a need, nobody should be armed simply because those they supervise are, that holds no logic at all.

entities.author: Ewan Ross
entities.text: Steven Blair For Francis Howell School Board it’s not about “trusting” though is it, his role doesn’t require a firearm. Ostensibly an SRO does (a solid argument can be made that arming SROs is stupid, but that isn’t a fight anyone is gonna actually win in the Midwest). Is there a need for the firearm to be present day to day? Is the individual patrolling school grounds? Are they doing the job of a supervisor and administrator, as their job title and description suggests, or are they doing the job of essentially a security guard?If the latter then hire them as a SRO and pay them as such and look for someone to head up security who isn’t so bonkers as to think they should be concealed carrying. If the former then really they cannot justify a need, and without a need the answer, with regards to the presence of a firearm, should always be no, regardless of how much you trust the individual.

entities.text: Becky Hormuth Hello Becky. We didn’t vote to let him carry a concealed weapon as Director of Safety and Security just because he wants to. You’re right that there are a lot of employees who won’t get something just because they want it. Basically, this position will train SRO’s for many ways of improving safety and security in the schools. To me, it would be odd for us to not trust a law enforcement officer Director of Safety and Security but trust the people they supervise. On the second point, I’d love to learn more. Am I hearing you correctly that your concern is the district paying stipends for employees with some additional responsibilities but not paying similar stipends to employees with equal amount of additional time?

entities.text: Steven Blair For Francis Howell School Board there are a list of things as an employee that I would like to have or get to do as well, yet I have had to learn more often than not, things don’t always get to be that way. Great life lesson! In all honesty, it was personally beyond frustrating to sit through the meeting last night. I myself, as many of my colleagues, put in long hours beyond the school day…just ask my husband…cause he’s not a big fan of it! So, it was very surprising to see in the budget that a certain group of educators will get compensated with an additional nice sized stipend next year. That role is a role I previously had the past 5 years. I definitely did do a lot of work outside of contract hours in that role, but I currently do as much or more in the classroom role I have now! I left 801 feeling so very undervalued and beyond frustrated!

entities.text: Ewan Ross 1- Yes. The first vote created the School Protection Officer as a possible role. We will change policy 1432 so that it is clear we are talking about the Director of Safety and Security who is a law enforcement officer. This person will have a full time director job and will not be spending all his time in schools. When he does, he wanted the ability to conceal and carry. At a later vote, we will decide whether to identify him as a SPO. Whenever we have a new Director of Safety and Security that person would also have to be approved to be a SPO since it’s an individual by individual basis. I hope this helps.

Must possess excellent communication and customer service skills• Must be highly organized, motivated and able to work on multiple tasks simultaneously• Ability to problem solve, use good judgment, and maintain effective relationships with staff, colleagues, students and community• Must have strong professional integrity and ability to maintain strict confidentiality• Must be able to effectively entities.text: Steven Blair For Francis Howell School Board If the Board has zero interest in having teachers, etc. carry weapons, why develop a Board Policy creating the opportunity for exactly that? The policy doesn't say this can only be used for law enforcement officers, but that it can be granted to teachers and administrators at the Board's discretion. Is it fair to say our Director of Safety and Security is a law enforcement officer, or is he a former LEO? It sounds like the Board is creating policy to accommodate one person, who (I think) hasn't even started yet.

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | Last Night’s Board Meeting took steps toward fulfilling our Strategic Plan which your can view here. https://www.fhsdschools.org/about/strategic-plan 1- We approved the designation of a School Protection Officer. A SPO is allowed through Missouri Statute 160.655 whixh allows a school board to designate a teacher or admin to carry a concealed firearm. All of School Resource Officers carry a weapon to protect the students at their school. This is not an open ended vote that creates a flood of staff members carrying guns. Conversations last night were clear that the only SPO will be our Director of Safety and Security who is a law enforcement officer who also trains local police departments. When he visits schools as part of his duties he will be allowed to conceal and carry. 2- Brain Pop. During the May Board Meeting, admin shared the reasons why Brain Pop is a valuable resource for teachers. We discussed those points and some concerns. We voted to approve the purchase of Brain Pop for the 25-26 School Year. 3- Budget - The main purpose for two June Board Meetings is to receive the full Budget proposal on June 5 so we can discuss it and approve the budget proposal, or a modified version, at the June 19 Board Meeting. The presentation had 70 slides I will share a summary and highlights in another post before June 19. 4- Libraries - During the May Board Meeting, admin shared recommendations from librarians regarding Policy 6310 which requires listing books before purchase. Those recommendations went to the policy committee who presented an updated version. The goal was to keep the Transparency value from the originals piece and to add Efficiency. We shared different opinions about the new proposed version. It was listed as First Read last night and will be up for a vote on June 19. Thank you everyone for showing your love for students by being engaged in what’s happening in Francis Howell. | a5DGOL8YI.com

entities.author: Jarrett Pillsbury
entities.text: Top fanSteven Blair For Francis Howell School Board Hi President Blair, I have a conflict and won't be able to attend the meeting. Can you tell us if there's new supporting evidence or data suggesting that the addition of SPOs will make the school environment safer? Most research shows a lack of effectiveness and the potential for added risks such as increased accidental discharges, mistaken identity, and escalation of violence. Alternate measures with more supporting data include providing for School Resource Officers, Threat Assessment Teams, and Mental Health Services. The National Association of School Resource Officers and the Major Cities Chiefs Association have both argued against such programs. If we want to make data driven decisions, I'm afraid I just don't see that in this instance and would recommend the Board vote this down in favor of other programs for which there is data to support a safer school environment. Thank you for reading.

entities.author: Steven Blair For Francis Howell School Board
entities.text: Additional information about the School Protection Officer agenda item, added to the agenda. Safety and Security is one of four pillars of the District’s strategic plan. The District has taken a number of steps recently to enhance safety measures across its 23 schools, including hiring a Director of Safety and Security with a law enforcement and military background. The Francis Howell School District has no interest in deputizing teachers to carry weapons. Even if the Board elects to authorize the District to designate SPOs, the Board must vote to approve each person individually. At this time, only one person is being considered based on their law enforcement experience and training. Votes involving individually identifiable personnel matters and personal information about employees happen in closed session to protect the privacy of the employee, in accordance with the law. Per state statute, employees seeking to be designated as an SPO must make a written request to the Superintendent, along with proof of ownership of a valid concealed carry endorsement or permit. They must also complete an approved SPO training program. SPOs are not permitted to allow any firearm or device out of their personal control while on school property.

entities.text: Shawn White Hello Shawn. We have a policy that residents of Francis Howell can sign up to be part of patron comments at a board meeting. The gentleman you’re referring to was not a resident. He was contacted the day before the meeting and given a chance to show proof he was a resident in Francis Howell. He did not show any evidence that he had established residence here so we told him ahead of time that he would not be allowed to speak during patron comments because he was not a patron. We followed the policy equally. Moments later a resident who is black spoke in patron comments because that person is a resident.The gentleman was not allowed to speak because they were not a resident and not because of their race. I know there could be misleading or incomplete info out there but I hope this additional background helps.

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | Memorial Day Idea - Building Empathy Building love and concern for others is important for a student’s development. This Memoriall Day, consider visiting a local cemetery for 30 minutes with your student(s). Visit the headstones that have an American Flag. By looking at the Date of Death, tell your kids if that person likely died in battle. Point out anything you can realistically guess by the Date of Death of their spouse, if it is a shared plot. Then, consider saying one of the following with your kids. 1- Thank you (insert name here) for serving our country. Or have them repeat after you. 2- Dear God. (Echo) For the life of ___________. (Echo), thank you. (Echo). Amen. (Echo). email. | xTaE8k.com

entities.authorKey: name:steven blair for francis howell school board
entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | Last Night. We followed an agenda to help us accomplish our Strategic Plan goals. Among other items, here are the highlights. - The Board approved a debt defeasance where we agreed to pay down $13,790,000 of principal. This comes from the pocket of money attached to debt service levy that cannot be used forth regular operating expenses. - The Board approved bids for FHHS asphalt, Hollenbeck roofing and Fairmount roofing. - Admin presented how Brain Pop helps supplement teacher instruction. The budget proposal on June 5th will include Brain Pop. - Admin presented ways that the spirit of 6310 aimed at increasing transparency for book purchases might be improved after talking with librarians. They will present those recommendations to Policy Committee. Policy Committee will present their suggested edits to the Board for First Read on June 5th. The goal is to keep the Transparency of 6310 and add Efficiency. - SM Wilson presented an update about the odor at FHN including steps taken and the new monitor readouts. Because the smell still occurs intermittently, they are working on next steps to present after they receive some information. - Admin presented an update on our Stategic Plan. It includes Four Pillars: Teachers and Learning, People and Workforce, Finance and Operation, Safety and Security. You can read more about them here. https://www.fhsdschools.org/about/strategic-plan Thank you, everyone! | p3SEM.com

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | Proud to cekebrate FHN Journalism Press Release From Nationals in Seattle: The Francis Howell North High School journalism staffs returned from a successful trip to their spring National High School Journalism Convention that was April 24-26 in Seattle. BEST OF SHOW Highlighting the awards for the staffs were their finishes in the Best of Show Competitions. All four publications placed in the Top 10! The Excalibur Yearbook placed 8th in their category. The North Star Newsmagazine placed 7th in the small schools category. FHNtodayTV staff placed 3rd in Broadcast News Shows and FHNtoday.com/FHNgameday.com brought home the Best of Show trophy placing first in small school websites. PACEMAKER That wasn’t the only award for FHNtoday.com/FHNgameday.com. The site also earned the prestigious Pacemaker Award, NSPA’s highest honor. It’s the 10th Pacemaker for the site in school history and brings the total number of Pacemakers for the program to 26. “Winning a prestigious award, such as the Pacemaker, is always such a huge win for the team,” FHNgameday Co-Editor-in-Chief said. “It’s a long and difficult process, and almost everyone on the staffs contribute to the site in some way. It’s just so nice to see everyone get recognized for all the hard work they put in all year to make the site the best it can be with photos, videos, stories and more.” FIRST AMENDMENT PRESS FREEDOM AWARD Francis Howell North was also recognized as one of only 21 schools in the country to earn the prestigious First Amendment Press Freedom Award. “I always take special pride in this award because it honors the school, the district and the students in the program for honoring and following the freedoms afforded in the First Amendment,” Media Adviser Aaron Manfull said. “It’s one of the many reasons this school is so special.” | zgNvz.com

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | Listen to this great story I just received: Sometimes, One Howell includes Ft. Zumwalt… President Blair: I wanted to share how impressed I was with the Howell High boys’ tennis team. They played our team here at FZWHS. My son who has unique learning needs is on our tennis team and was ecstatic to see one of his friends from your school coming to play with us. Arrangements were made so that my son could play a singles match against your student, Jack Tilton. My son is pretty small for his age and is far from the strongest player on the team, although he does bring a tremendous amount of enthusiasm to the team. It would have been easy for Jack to decline my son’s invitation to play and even easier for Jack’s teammates to pick on my child. Instead Jack happily accepted the opportunity and six of the players from your team watched the entire game from outside the fence while loudly and enthusiastically cheering on my child AND their teammate. These young men were the epitome of not just acceptance but true inclusion. My son lost his match because Jack treated him like any other opponent rather than watering it down for him. The score mattered little to him because he was so excited to have had such great kids cheering for him and encouraging him. What probably felt small and simple to them meant the world to my kid and we are so grateful to know that such wonderful humans are tomorrow’s leaders. Please share with your tennis coach and these young people how impressed we are with them. Let them know that their kind gesture, their patience, and their willingness to share his joy in the game will not soon be forgotten. Someone shared this picture of Jack and my son just before they played. These two boys have grown up together in church since they were two. This is a picture of true friendship. With Deepest Gratitude, Aimee Robertson, BCBA, LBA | OafUFgcTU1.com

entities.author: Kristina Burke
entities.text: Just want to point out that our PAT group is amazing too. My son has been a part of the program for years, and for the past 2 years while I fought my own cancer battle, our PAT teacher was beyond wonderful. Her care and compassion for our son and our family during a very stressful time was amazing. And she always provided reassurance for me when I was concerned with how long it took for my kid to potty train while I was going through treatments as well as providing resources and guidance with other developments that we felt were taking longer or concerned about during that time. Our kiddo is more than ready for kindergarten next fall and she has been a big part of that preparation.

entities.author: Rebecca Becky
entities.text: While my son doesn’t have cancer he was born with a mixed bag of medical issues that took hundreds of doctor’s visits with specialists and dozens of surgeries and he will always have a long road ahead of him medically speaking. From First Steps to Preschool to elementary school and middle school and high school every single teacher, every counselor……every single year they have poured their love and concern into his growth and development. Without the amazingly talented, highly skilled teachers he would not be where he is today. He was offered a good amount of scholarships from Missouri S&T and will continue his education beyond graduation. I thank everyone who has held him up -basically since birth.

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | “Before cancer, Benny was a regular kid. He was intense- he loved to play hockey and run and get dirty. Benny was diagnosed with Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia on January 10th, 2022. He could barely walk down the hallway from exhaustion. {His mom} drove Benny to Cardinal Glennon ER, and that is the hospital where we lived for an entire month, filled with chemotherapy and steroids and blood transfusions and an endless pit of confusion and fear. His birthday is January 19, so he had his 4th birthday in the hospital. He was supposed to start kindergarten for the 23-24 school year, but for safety concerns, due to his compromised immune system, they advised us to wait a year. Enter Ms. Caswell. “Ms Caswell needs to be protected at all costs. She saved us. We had become an unsure, insecure family. We knew we had so much to be grateful for, but we still hadn’t found our feet. From the very first day, he came home smiling. He LOVED her. She was always there to him cheer him on. But on March 18th of this year, marking Benny being an entire year chemo-free, she gave Benny a chance to tell his story to his peers. All the kindergarten classes got together and listened to Benny explain why March 18th is such a special day for him. Not only did that moment mean… well, everything… but to think of Benny having the CONFIDENCE to do that- I want everyone to understand that if it had not been for HER support, HER attitude, HER innate ability to incite courage and strength into these tiny humans, we would not be where we are. She has allowed him to become the person he is meant to be. She’s changed our family in ways I can’t even describe. I think we all grew up a little bit. We all learned how to let Benny be Benny, because we learned from her.” - Jesse (Benny’s Mom) ———————- I wanted to celebrate Benny being one year cancer free and all the courage he displayed. I wanted to celebrate Ms. Sarah Caswell for being a teacher who cared for the whole student. AND.. I want to let you know that while Ms. Caswell is extraordinary, she is not alone. No matter your kid’s age, what school your kid attends, and what your kid goes through there will be teachers, staff, admin, and counselors there to care for them, too. | j8Vgp.com

entities.author: Grace Martin
entities.text: Steven Blair For Francis Howell School Board the school has a code of conduct that all parents and kids sign each school year and nothing is done when the code is broken. The anti racism resolution was hanging in the buildings and we had problems. I don’t see how hanging that back up will make a difference.The ones that get bullied stand up for themselves and are the ones that get in trouble. That needs to change. Maybe we can enforce the code of conduct, have actual consequences and follow through. Stop giving so many chances to these kids. Enforce the rules that are already in place and focus on things like teachers. Also, the smell at the high school where many of our kids are getting sick, but being dismissed when they say anything. That feels like a big lawsuit waiting to happen and should be the number one priority at the moment.

entities.author: Beth Moede Abraham
entities.text: Lisa Kramer I hear your frustration and agree with your belief that this resolution needs to be reinstated. I also understand the new Directors (and ones new to their positions) are striving not to steamroll the patrons of the district with their personal beliefs (as the previous 2 boards did). I am grateful Director Blair put this on the May agenda - which is as soon as he could. He only had 2 days between bring appointed Board President and this meeting. Had he barged ahead with ANYTHING in just two days he would have broken trust with the community. I have faith that this topic is very core to the beliefs of the new board majority and it will be quickly dealt with. Give them a month or two to get things working. We do want the due process - it will legitimize future actions.

entities.author: Steven Blair For Francis Howell School Board
entities.text: Lisa Kramer Hello Lisa. Thank you for sharing these thoughts. We also ran on bringing normalcy to the Board. Adding any of these to last night’s agenda would have made a last minute agenda change that has recently caused a number of problems. In May, we will listen to the professionals and what they want regarding Brain Pop and 6310 and respond accordingly. The Anti Racism Resolution means a lot to a large number of people. It’s one of the top reasons I moved to Francis Howell. There’s a chance that we realize we need a policy instead of a resolution or a statement or a number of other options. There’s also a chance that using the exact same language will cause problems down the road. I was asked by another board member to present a next step at the May Meeting and I will be glad to do so.

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | Here are some highlights from last night. 1- We approved 25-26 and 26-27 school calendars. These calendars follow state rules regarding start date, keep Fall Break, and have first semester end before Winter Break. 2- We approved the purchase of 4000 chromebooks and celebrated how admin saved taxpayers a significant amount of money before tariffs with China kicked in. 3- We heard SM Wilson’s plans to address the odor at FHN through testing happening today with multiple companies and general contractors involved. We also communicated our direction if today’s work doesn’t produce an answer. 4- We approved members for the employee insurance committee and policy committee. 5- We reviewed all the steps being made to respond to the state audit. 6-The student representative from Saeger asked a number of great questions and added to the discussion. 7- We requested admin have discussions with librarians about policy 6310 to see what’s working and what might need improvement. Admin will present ideas at the May Meeting. Policy 6310 requires a specific chronicling of all books being purchased by schools. 8- We requested a similar presentation regarding the Brain Pop resource. Admin will share at the May Meeting the results of conversations with staff. They would then share whether they want lBrain Pop to be added to the budget we vote on in June. 9- I was asked to present a pathway for discussing the Resolution Against Racism in a different setting than a regular board meeting. This could be a work session, board retreat, or perhaps a different format. I will bring my recommended option to the May Meeting. The full board shared interest for 7, 8, and 9. I appreciate VP Gryder, Treasurer Owens, Directors Harmon, Oelke, Ponder, and Puszkar for their leadership last night. | 13U8mTO9ah.com

entities.author: Ren Boehms Adams
entities.text: Top fanKara Elms they keep cutting staff. In my ten years in the district, I’ve seen them cut so many supports because we simply don’t have the staff to cover it. Since study skills classes typically have smaller class sizes and focus on specialized instruction, they are more vulnerable to cuts. If fewer teachers are available, schools must consolidate classes, which can lead to the elimination of electives or support classes like study skills in favor of larger, more general classes that serve more students. We need a tax levy and a board that understands this is our district’s priority, not culture wars.

entities.text: I will also add- should this change in policy take effect, I believe you will see many kids decrease the amount of honors and AP classes they are taking. It would NOT be worth the stress of having to worry about taking 7 finals that all potentially counted for 20% of your grade. I'm a HUGE fan of AP and honors classes! Both of my older two kids have entered college with over 30 credits thanks to AP. That's a year's worth of school, essentially saving our family 25% on college. I want students to look forward to a high level of rigor and challenge but not at the cost of their mental and emotional well being if they had to take 7 finals that counted for 20% of their grades in a 3 day period.

Additionally, I find it interesting that this policy is being voted on last minute at a work session instead of a regularly schedule board meeting. Are policies generally voted on during work sessions? If it was such a great policy, one would think it would be passed regardless of the makeup of the board.

entities.author: Steven Blair For Francis Howell School Board
entities.text: Severe Weather Email from FHSD District Office. (Read for details regarding how today’s weather might impact pickup and buses) FHSD Staff and Community: The National Weather Service (NWS) in St. Louis has advised school districts in our area to expect severe weather this afternoon. Our region is under an enhanced risk for severe weather, including high winds, hail and possible tornadoes. While exact timing is difficult to predict, the NWS believes the greatest likelihood for severe storms to develop will be between 1:00 p.m. and 4:00 p.m. for our area, which could impact dismissal procedures. We will be carefully monitoring the weather as the day progresses. Here are a few things for you to know: · Training and Drills - We have weather-related safety plans in place to keep students and staff safe while they're at school. Our school and district leaders are trained in tornado preparedness and response, and our students practice tornado drills every school year so they know what to do during a tornado warning. · Tornado Watch Versus Tornado Warning - According to the NWS, a tornado watch means tornadoes are possible in and near the watch area; it does not mean a tornado will occur. A tornado warning is more serious; it means a tornado has been sighted or indicated by weather radar, and requires immediate action. During a tornado warning, all staff and students are required to seek shelter in a designated tornado-safe area. · Tornado Sirens - In our area, tornado sirens sound for the entire county when a tornado is indicated via radar or by a trained spotter. Because we are a geographically large county, the actual area of rotation may be close to some schools, but far from others. Our procedures require that all students and staff seek shelter in their designated tornado-safe area when the sirens sound. The tornado siren sounds for three minutes, and will sound again if the warning is extended. · All Clear Signal - District administrators consult the National Weather Service and/or local law enforcement for the tornado warning expiration and all-clear notice. The siren silencing does not mean the warning has ended. After the all clear is given, students may be picked up by parents. · Student Dismissal - Please refrain from coming to school to pick up your child during a tornado warning; students will not be dismissed until the all-clear is given. Our protocols require staff and students to seek shelter in their designated tornado-safe space inside the building, away from doors and windows. This means that staff will not be available to answer phone calls or open doors during an active tornado warning. · Buses - Students will not be released to school buses during an active tornado warning. Buses already en route when a tornado warning is issued will proceed to the nearest school or other predetermined safe location to seek shelter. Bus drivers and students will remain at that location until the warning has expired and the all-clear is given. Depending on the timing of the weather event, buses may run later than normal. Parents of students who walk or bike home are encouraged to have an alternative transportation plan in place when severe weather is expected. · Communication - Communication may be limited during an active tornado warning due to the supervision of students and the technology limitations severe weather may present. As always, we will communicate any changes in regular routines with families via the SchoolMessenger notification system and the District website as soon as it is safe to do so. Thank you for your support and cooperation as we navigate today's possible severe weather event. Read more about our tornado procedures on the District website.

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | Francis Howell schools are closed Tuesday, February 18 due to hazardous road conditions across the District. All classes are canceled. Preschool and Vacation Station are also closed and will not operate. All after school and evening activities at elementary and middle schools are canceled. Activity Directors will work collaboratively with District personnel to determine high school events by midday. Each AD will communicate with head coaches and sponsors regarding their respective sport or activity. High school families will receive updates from their child’s coach as warranted. More info: fhsdschools.org/programsservices/facilities-operations/weather-guidelines | d2NIJ.com

entities.author: Sherri Agee Kulpa
entities.text: As a community member, I'm heartened to see the Francis Howell community values diversity and wants a welcoming school district for all. Although our district is predominantly white, a recent survey showed that mostly white respondents believe diversity and inclusion are crucial - ranking 'District's Understanding/Support for Diversity' and 'Racial Equity and Social Justice' as the 2nd and 3rd most needed areas for improvement, just behind staff morale. Moreover, nearly half of respondents felt the district isn't effectively implementing social justice and equity practices for students. I urge the board to consider these findings when selecting our next district leader and when supporting the new superintendent in making Francis Howell a great place to learn and work for everyone.

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | District Superintendent Survey Results. (1370 Responses!!!) On Monday, the search firm School Exec Connect shared the below results from their survey and focus groups to the School Board. You can see the report here. It includes the info about who responded to the survey, opinions on District strengths and challenges, and ends with a profile of desired superintendent candidates. Most steps from here are deliberately closed and confidential. This confidentiality is important to ensure the largest amount of candidates apply. The search firm will collect candidates’ interest, vet them, and bring a list of 5-7 candidates to the Board. Through interviews we will reduce the number to three and then undergo another round of interviews. This timeline hopefully produces an excellent candidate that the Board can hire and introduce to the community at the March Board Meeting. https://resources.finalsite.net/images/v1738094621/fhsdschoolsorg/yaxvjwtdhy85p2ilm1ti/Francis-Howell-Community-Engagement-Report.pdf | 8LQttIgmdG.com

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | Independence families: I am thrilled to share with you that Dr. Connie Buckman will be joining the Independence family as an assistant principal next school year! Dr. Buckman currently serves as the District’s Chief Academic Officer. Prior to that, she supported the professional development of teachers across the District as the Director of Adult Learning. She began her teaching career at Becky-David Elementary and spent three years at Independence as a Literacy Coach. We are very excited to welcome her back to the building. I could not have asked for a more capable or qualified leader to join our administration team. Her expertise, knowledge and skills will help our building continue to meet the needs of our students, staff, and families. Many of you will recognize her familiar face, as she is an Independence parent (her daughter, Emily, is a 4th grader this year). Dr. Buckman will continue to serve as Chief Academic Officer through June 30 and will transition to her assistant principal role on July 1 as I begin my tenure as principal. You can read more about Dr. Buckman’s decision to join our team on the District website. https://www.fhsdschools.org/news/meet-fhsd/~board/district-news/post/district-to-begin-search-for-new-academic-leader-as-chief-academic-officer-transitions-to-a-new-role-for-25-26 Thank you, Jana Schultz Assistant Principal | J2CHi.com

TONIGHT Staff at 4:30pm Community Members at 6pm ———- FHSD STAFF AND COMMUNITY MEMBERS: The Francis Howell School District Board of Education has begun the search process for a new superintendent. The District selected SCHOOL EXEC CONNECT, an educational search firm, to assist us in this process. If you would like to provide input on the District’s strengths, challenges, and the characteristics the next superintendent should possess, the SCHOOL EXEC CONNECT consultants invite you to attend an open forum this evening. Open Forum for Francis Howell staff members: Tuesday, Jan. 21, 2025 4:30 to 5:30 p.m. Board Rooms 1D/E 801 Corporate Centre Drive O’Fallon, MO 63368 Open Forum for Francis Howell community members: Tuesday, Jan. 21, 2025 6:00 to 7:00 p.m. Board Rooms 1D/E 801 Corporate Centre Drive O’Fallon, MO 63368 Findings from the survey, the open forums, and several focus group conversations will be used to develop a New Superintendent Profile that will be reported to the Board on January 27, 2025. Please feel free to contact the consultants assisting us if you have any questions or comments regarding the search: Dr. Kevin O’Mara Ms. Diane Robertson We look forward to your input as we search for a new superintendent to lead the Francis Howell School District. | ZZrxAgp.com

entities.text: Top fanFirst is this. . . "First, I must confess that over the past few years I have been gravely disappointed with the white moderate. I have almost reached the regrettable conclusion that the Negro's great stumbling block in his stride toward freedom is not the White Citizen's Counciler or the Ku Klux Klanner, but the white moderate, who is more devoted to 'order' than to justice; who prefers a negative peace which is the absence of tension to a positive peace which is the presence of justice; who constantly says: 'I agree with you in the goal you seek, but I cannot agree with your methods of direct action'; who paternalistically believes he can set the timetable for another man's freedom; who lives by a mythical concept of time and who constantly advises the Negro to wait for a 'more convenient season.'""Shallow understanding from people of good will is more frustrating than absolute misunderstanding from people of ill will. Lukewarm acceptance is much more bewildering than outright rejection."And this. . . "Human progress never rolls in on wheels of inevitability;"Both are hard for me to accept but I feel I'm beginning to understand both more clearly.

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | Schools are closed on Monday. Here is the email sent by Francis Howell to parents/guardians. Look closely at the details regarding high school students and finals. Our school calendar does not include a built in snow day, so tomorrow is an AMI Day which stands for Alternate Methods of Instruction. Students should follow the instructions here: www.fhsdschools.org/ami ———- FHSD staff and families: Due to the ongoing Winter Storm and hazardous road conditions across the District, Monday will be an AMI Day (Alternative Methods of Instruction). All Francis Howell schools will be closed and students will learn remotely. Please refer to the snow day packet distributed earlier this year or visit www.fhsdschools.org/ami for links and more information. Preschool and Vacation Station will also be closed on Monday. All after school and evening activities at elementary and middle schools are canceled. Activity Directors will work collaboratively with District personnel to make determinations regarding high school level events by midday Monday. Each AD will communicate with head coaches and sponsors regarding their respective sport. High school families will receive updates from their child’s coach as warranted. We will continue to closely monitor the impact of the Winter Storm Warning issued by the National Weather Service, and will communicate any additional schedule changes as early as possible. FHSD staff should refer to the snow day guidelines document for information about working on inclement weather days. For more information on snow closure procedures, visit the District website. FINAL EXAM SCHEDULE IMPACTS (This information is relevant for high school students, as well as middle school students enrolled in high school level courses). Students enrolled in high school courses are scheduled to take final exams this week on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday. If we are able to have in-person learning on Tuesday, we will proceed with this exam schedule. This will allow students to study independently during tomorrow’s AMI day, and have time on Tuesday to receive additional support from teachers prior to exams beginning on Wednesday, January 8. Assuming we only need to utilize one AMI Day this week, the second semester will begin as scheduled on Tuesday, January 14. IF THE DISTRICT HAS TWO AMI DAYS THIS WEEK (MONDAY AND TUESDAY) If weather or road conditions require the District to utilize an additional AMI day on Tuesday, January 7, final exams will be pushed back by one school day. This would allow Wednesday to be an in-person review day, with final exams on Thursday, January 9, Friday, January 10 and Tuesday, January 14. In this scenario, the second semester will begin on Wednesday, January 15. (Due to a pre-scheduled College and Career event on Tuesday, January 14 , Francis Howell North students would follow a modified schedule, with final exams this week on Thursday and Friday, and Wednesday of the following week.) Please note that no decisions have been made about using an AMI day on Tuesday, but we want families and students to know that we have a plan in place should we need it. Additional information about final exam schedules will come directly from the impacted schools as needed. Please do everything possible to keep you and your family safe and warm during this weather event, and we look forward to welcoming students back to school when the roads are clear in all areas of the District. Thank you, FHSD Communications | dIETYk7IG.com

entities.author: Lisa Kramer
entities.text: So with this extraordinarily small window of time, how much input and well/roundedness of input will be lost due to the right people being unavailable to participate. Moving on to the actual screening, interviewing…..Albeit, the FHSD5 gets their panties in a wad talking about equity & fairness, but it’s a big problem for me as a taxpayer when we rush through a $2XXk salary plus comp pkg hire because these type of Herculean hire timelines almost always mean not every member of the hiring team will be available to interview each candidate, and that results in inconsistencies in the evaluation process & a less comprehensive understanding of each applicants qualifications.And you intend to interview 5-7 candidates? What happens when the most qualified candidate on paper can’t accommodate the 1 hour/1 day offered her for an interview? We just going to eliminate her from the pool? Also, spring breaks - board going to cancel theirs?. This is a face to face type interview.

Here’s a few highlights. 1- The Board agreed to have the names of the candidates be held confidential to encourage more applicants. 2- The process will include considerable input by others. We will have an online survey and a number of focus groups led by the firm. This will include groups of teachers, staff, high school students, community members, and more. I will share more information about how those groups will be selected. 3-Information from all these sources will help create a profile of what we are looking for in a new superintendent. 4- We hope to receive all candidate’s resume, etc by February 14. School Exec Connect will give 5-7 candidates for the Board to interview. From there, we will narrow candidates down planning on deciding in early March. 5- We plan to have a great superintendent to announce at the March Board Meeting. 6-This is a short process, but it hits all the important steps of a longer process. No steps are being skipped. 7-I agree with the timeline to get a superintendent chosen in mid-March. This will help recruit new teachers while they are making decisions in Spring. It will also give time for an incoming superintendent to learn from our outgoing superintendent and set them up for success. I will keep sharing updates here as well. It’s a big moment for our district. I am hopeful that the process will reveal an amazing superintendent for Francis Howell. https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=smrwyfvS_4E&pp=ygUsZnJhbmNpcyBob3dlbGwgc2Nob29sIGRpc3RyaWN0IGJvYXJkIG1lZXRpbmc%3D | KAHNrEiiM.com

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | Lego Robotics I have coached Lego Robotics for three years. Our regional qualifier is next Saturday, December 14. These ten students have learned coding skills and a lot of ‘soft’ skills like teamwork, resilience, and what Lego calls ‘gracious professionalism.’ This team includes 4+ religions including non religious, multiple ethnicities, skill sets, personality types, and growing edges. It is a great sample of what we hope every student experiences at FHSD and I’m really proud of the growth I have seen in each of them. Cheer on our team ‘Kraken Crew’ and others this upcoming weekend. | xDDSNBUD.com
